steps: Scoped the population. NS-11 section 2 measures service to the dealer network, and the data dictionary states a movement is either a dealer delivery or a replenishment transfer to another RDC, with the ship-to master carrying `dealer_kind` of RDC on the internal points. Excluding transfers leaves 40,348 consignments in the prior-year half and 53,847 in the current one.

Measured the move on that population: on-time 97.137 percent against 89.002, a fall of 8.135 points. On every movement rather than every consignment it reads 8.700, which is the first figure that goes wrong if the transfers are left in.

Rebuilt the lane band through the distance reference and the band edges the service catalogue carries, then pulled contracted transit days for that service and band from the catalogue version in force.

Rebuilt the tender date from the dispatch wave schedule, and recovered how the day outbound positions are filled, because the counterfactuals turn on which trailer freight rides. The published cutoffs alone reproduce the recorded tender offset on 165,064 of 167,397 movements, and the cutoffs with the position clause in the capacity file reproduce all 167,397. Five rival fills were run against the same ledger and the best of them reproduces 166,208.

Established the clock against the closed 2025 claim year. From trailer close reproduces 4,020 of 4,125 dispositions and 3,342 of 4,125 credits. From tender but charging the carrier for the consignee's own receiving restriction reproduces 4,054 and 3,873. From tender net of consignee restriction days reproduces **all 4,125 of both**.

Measured what the night trailer actually costs before pricing the wave structure, because a day trailer is only worth an operating day if the day is not given back downstream. Excess over contracted transit, day tender against night tender, splits absolutely on the lane band: every interline cell 0.68 to 0.86 of a day in the night trailer's favour, every direct city cell between -0.04 and -0.03.

Priced each of the six standing conditions, returned to its prior-year level with nothing else changed, which for the wave-side conditions means the prior-year schedule, the contracted positions and the consolidation day together: F1 **6.599**, F4 **1.391**, F6 **0.433**, F2 0.407, F3 0.078, F5 0.002. On the tender day alone F6 reads 2.256, which is where the ranking changes.

Applied NS-11 section 3. The carrier condition is already answered by the service credit terms in the carrier agreements and the claim year shows those terms settling, so it is minuted with its figure and is not funded. Nothing else on the list has a supplier agreement behind it.
Recommendation: F4, dealer receiving conversion, at 1.4 points, leading the next fundable condition by 3.21x, and it survives holding out each distribution centre and each service class in turn. ---

critical_components: The population is **consignments to the dealer network**, which is not the same as the rows in the movement table. The table carries replenishment transfers between the four RDCs as well as dealer deliveries, **12,043 of them across the extract**, 2,238 in the prior-year half and 5,584 in the current one. They run 79 percent on the two longest lane bands and they miss at 17.7 percent against 11.0, so leaving them in overstates the comparison. In scope: **40,348** and **53,847** consignments; on-time **97.137 percent** falling to **89.002**, a decline of **8.135 points** against 8.700 on the whole movement book.

The contractual clock runs from **tender**, not from trailer close, and the only place it is recoverable is the closed claim year: of three readings swept, exactly one reproduces the settled file at **4,125 of 4,125 dispositions and 4,125 of 4,125 credit amounts**. Two claims identical on every column the file shows settle **3.00x apart**, at $18.75 and $56.25, separated only by which trailer they rode.

**The largest repair is not the recovery line.** Carrier line-haul performance returns **6.599 points**, four and a half times the largest fundable condition and more than everything else together several times over. NS-11 section 3 leaves a condition already answered by a term in a supplier agreement to that term, every carrier contract in the reference carries service credit terms, and the closed claim year shows those terms live with **4,020 claims accepted and $253,432.75 settled**. No other condition on the list has a counterparty agreement behind it at all.

**The night trailer is a consolidation, not a late day trailer, and on the interline lanes it gives the operating day back.** The wave consolidation moved the in-scope book from 13.7 percent on the night trailer to 56.7, and that trailer tenders one operating day after it closes, so priced on the tender day alone the wave structure is worth **2.256 points** and leads everything else the plan can fund. Measured against contracted transit, day tender minus night tender, **all twelve interline cells give back between 0.68 and 0.86 of an operating day and all four direct city cells give back nothing, between -0.04 and -0.03**. Netting that off leaves the wave structure at **0.433 points**, second of the five conditions the review can fund. ---
submission.recommendation: **Put F4, dealer receiving conversion, on the FY27 recovery line.** It accounts for **1.4 points** of the 8.1 point fall in on-time delivery to the dealer network, and it leads the next thing the review can fund by **3.21x**. Not F1, carrier line-haul performance, which returns more than any other condition at 6.6 points, four and a half times the largest thing the plan can fund and four fifths of the whole decline, and which the review minutes rather than funds, because the carrier agreements already carry the remedy and the closed claim year shows it being paid. Not F6, dispatch wave structure, which is worth 2.3 points if the tender day is priced on its own and 0.4 once the day the consolidation trailer gives back is taken off it. Not F2, lane and volume mix, at 0.4 points, not F3, cross-dock re-handling, at 0.1, and not F5, order intake drift, at 0.0. ---

submission.objective_tag: Data Extraction & Conformation (ETL / Pipeline Build).
steps: Read the fixed width manifest extract as the population. It carries 4,834 container movements for the window, while the TMS event feed only ever mentions 4,041 units, so 793 movements are missing from the feed everything else in the folder is built on.

Conformed the two event vocabularies into one. The TMS feed writes numeric date types and facility local time in two different string formats, one of them the Oracle DD-MON-YYYY form, and the carrier status pull writes mnemonics and UTC, so the pull has to be localised through each facility's IANA zone before any day is counted. That gives 47,163 distinct events covering all 4,834 movements, and the 367 movements present in both feeds agree to the second once converted, which is what proves the conversion.

Resolved terms per carrier. Amendment 7 Schedule A names Nordline, Talara and Ostmark, and its clause 9.2 leaves the rest of the tariff in force, so demurrage for those three runs from the vessel discharge complete event with four days free, per diem runs from out-gate with three days free, and Kestrel and Cordova take the tariff's six and six. That puts 751 of the 976 accrued charge rows on amendment terms, worth USD 692,256.90, and 225 on the tariff, worth USD 191,732.65. Schedule rates come from the rate workbook on the effective period of the first chargeable day, which puts the 2027 revision on everything that starts in the quarter.

Recovered the per diem stop rule from the closed 2026 audit file. Running the filed rules alone reproduces 163 of the 209 settled day counts, and the 46 that miss are all per diem lines on units that were turned away at a return location. Sweeping every partition of the ten refusal codes, exactly one set (RJ12, RJ18, RJ21, RJ27, RJ33) reproduces all 98 settled per diem cases, and those five codes are the ones describing a depot that could not receive rather than a unit that was not fit to hand back.

Checked the recovered rule against the pair the audit file makes hardest. NDLU1458224 and NDLU1471890 travelled on one bill of lading, one booking, the same vessel, the same terminal and the same equipment class, out-gated on 8 September 2026 and were both accepted back on 26 September, and the carrier billed both 15 per diem days. They settled at 8 days and 15 days, USD 1,500.40 against USD 4,150.30. Nothing visible at movement level separates them, and only the refusal reason on the intervening presentations does.
Built the conformed charge table at one row per movement per charge code, 9,511 rows, with 157 rows held back where no clock had started by the close date.

Applied the close instruction. Charge rows whose carrier invoice has already posted to accounts payable come out, which is 3,244 rows, 5,291 rows carry no billable day at all, and 976 rows across 815 movements remain.
Priced the 3,645 remaining billable days through the band structure that applies to each row. The accrual is USD 883,989.55, or USD 883,990 in whole dollars.

critical_components: The population is the 4,834 container movements on the inbound manifest extract, of which 793 were booked direct with the carrier, never landed in the TMS feed at all, and are recoverable only from the carrier status pull.

Nordline, Talara and Ostmark price under Service Contract Amendment No. 7, so their demurrage free time is four calendar days running from completion of vessel discharge operations rather than six days from each unit's own lift, and their chargeable days escalate to 2.20 and then 3.40 times the schedule rate. Kestrel and Cordova are not party to the amendment and stay on the published tariff.

The per diem clock stops at the first return presentation the depot refused for a reason inside its own control. No shipped document states this. It is recovered from the 209 closed 2026 audit cases, where exactly one of the 1,024 possible partitions of the ten refusal reason codes reproduces all 98 settled per diem day counts.

The accrual scope at the close date is every charge row carrying billable days whose carrier invoice has not yet posted, so the 3,244 already invoiced rows drop out and the clocks still running on 31 March accrue up to that date, which is 125 units on hire on the street plus 114 still inside the terminal.
submission.recommendation: We should book USD 883,990 at the 31 March 2027 close as the ocean equipment charge accrual, which is USD 883,989.55 to the cent. The figure is 815 container movements carrying 3,645 billable days, split USD 414,632.50 terminal demurrage and USD 469,357.05 equipment per diem. It is not USD 1,267,221.90, which is what a complete and correctly priced pipeline produces if the per diem clock is left running to the day each unit was finally accepted back. It is not USD 1,119,879.90, which is that same figure with the units still on the street and still inside the terminal at the close date dropped for want of a second endpoint. It is not USD 653,614.20, which is what you get pricing every carrier off the published tariff. And it is not USD 575,490.20, which is the number that falls out of the TMS event feed on its own, priced off the tariff, and is 35 percent short.

steps: Read the two revenue extracts by column name, because the 2026 to 2027 file came off the legacy system semicolon separated with a comma decimal mark in Latin-1 and the 2028 file came off the replacement portal with `turnover`, `purchases`, `activity_class_2012` and `district` renamed. Value added is turnover less purchases: 19,267 rows read as filed.
Took the highest version of each filer and period: 340 superseded rows dropped, 18,927 delivered figures.

Parsed the fixed-width register off its own header and attributed each return across the filer's local units live on the last day of the period, in proportion to registered employment, each unit carrying its own district and activity class. Quarantined value with no register cover or falling outside a Basin district. Loaded plus rejected equals source exactly, and the 2028 panel is 4,049,979.3 thousand florins.

Compared it against the published output series for 2028, 4,873,320.8 thousand florins. The series release note says it covers every producing local unit whether or not the enterprise files and that the sub-threshold part is the Board's own estimate, so the 823,341.5 difference is that estimate, and the advocates' case for lifting the panel is a case about coverage, not about the charge.

Settled what the charge is on before arguing coverage. Schedule 1 charges the returns of scheme producers, a term with no operational content anywhere in the pack, so rebuilt the previous cycle on each candidate basis against the Fund's settled acknowledgement of 1,950.66: the whole panel gives 4,795.88, a uniform lift 5,786.87, a group by group lift 6,009.05, each matching zero of the twelve division rows. The recorded obligation is far smaller than every candidate, so the description excludes filers.

Tried the natural description first and let the file refuse it. An enterprise-size ceiling on the filer's own register employment at each period end fits at no ceiling from 30 to 400: at best three of twelve rows reproduce, and the nine broken rows are all too high, so producers the Fund did not charge are still in the base, and they are not separable by size or turnover, because in each broken division chargeable producers sit above them on both.

Followed the overhang into the register's participation extract. Every uncharged small filer is held, above one half, by an enterprise that is over any plausible ceiling. Re-ran the sweep with each filer tested on the employment of its control-linked group: every ceiling from 193 to 209 reproduces all twelve rows to the cent. The recorded 15 per cent stake the Fund charged kills counting minority stakes, and the linked pair the Fund charged kills excluding on a bare link, so the description aggregates the control-linked group, ignores minority stakes, and applies return period by return period.

Applied the description to 2028. No filer's linked employment sits inside the corridor in any quarter, so ceilings 193 and 209 return identical division tables, and chargeable value added is 1,197,271.4 thousand florins, against 4,049,979.3 returned.
Applied the banded rates: the provision is 1,623.03 thousand florins, of which 57.4 per cent falls on the three divisions in band S, and division 25 carries 28.2 per cent, the largest single part.
Certification: 1,623 thousand florins.

steps: Parsed the legacy fixed width extract at the offsets its record layout publishes and the portal export's nested versions and lines, giving 99,664 version level cost records across two subrecipient id schemes and two award id schemes.

Resolved the two award key schemes through the migration key map, which is the only file in the bundle that maps them, and collapsed the overlap. 34,886 cost lines were present twice, once under a legacy award key and once under a portal one, because the portal backloaded each subrecipient's year to date history when it onboarded, so every pre onboarding period of an onboarded award sits in both systems. The two copies agree on all 34,886 shared lines, on amount, version status, submission date and acceptance date, so it does not matter which one is kept.

Took each award and reporting period at the report version accepted on or before that period's certification deadline, which the fiscal calendar publishes per period. That is the version the period settled against, and a version accepted after the deadline is a statement about a period that had already closed. Reported programme expenditure on that basis is USD 22,355,271.73.

Joined the cost code crosswalk on local cost code **and** programme, taking the programme from the award. Four shared cost centres are used under all four programmes and carry a different Fund category under each, so a join on the code alone fans the amounts out to USD 28,032,444.78. Collapsing that fan out to one mapping per code gives USD 9,069,536.67, and restricting the join to codes with a single mapping gives USD 3,985,813.23. Both of those are wrong and neither is obviously wrong.

Kept only the eight categories the grant agreement makes the Fund chargeable for, which held back USD 7,250,358.40 across 13,695 lines of match, other funder and non allowable cost that the subrecipients report on the same form.

Recovered the eligibility rule from the 240 closed FY2025 determinations. The agreement states that expenditure is Fund certifiable where it meets the standard the fiscal agent applies on review and that each closed review records the amount finally allowed, so those reviews are the record of what the term means, but no document anywhere states the test the reviewer applies. The test is that a cost is certifiable only where its Fund category already carried an approved budget line on the day the cost was incurred, so a category added to an award by amendment part way through the year does not reach back over the costs already booked against it. That rule reproduces all 240 determinations exactly to the cent, and it holds back USD 3,824,955.20 across 7,830 lines of FY2026 cost.
Certified figure: **USD 11,279,958.13**.

steps: Loaded the accounts payable ledger, 19,366 lines, parsing each provider's own date convention on its own shape, seven providers filing ISO and seven filing the finance system's DD-MON-YYYY default, and confirmed the line counts agree with the delivery log exactly and that no date is left unparsed.

Read the chart of accounts as an effective dated table rather than a code lookup, resolving each payment against the row in force on the day its warrant cleared. Three code strings, `01HSAF1`, `05HSAF1` and `09HSAF1`, carry two rows each with disjoint effective periods and different providers and funders either side of 1 December 2026.

Resolved the re-delivered months as an upsert on the warrant, ordered by the delivery log's filed date, because 2,198 of the re-delivered lines carry a corrected cost centre rather than a copy of the line they replace: 2,502 lines superseded, 16,864 remain.

Reconciled the load to the finance system's general ledger, which is one row per accounting period per funding source per activity on the cash basis. It ties to the cent in all 85 cells, and it does not tie under either flat reading of the chart or under any of the three wrong ways of handling the re-delivery, which is what settles both of those steps without any rule needing to be quoted.

Scoped to the Fund's direct financial assistance, which excludes the other three funders in the same ledger and the staff delivered service centres that are recovered through the administrative allocation: 6,118 lines held back, worth USD 6,023,991.86.

Measured the operating year against the period each payment covers rather than the date the warrant cleared, taking the window from the operating year start to the cut the renewal notice names: a further 1,192 lines held back, worth USD 1,470,360.98, most of it April and May rent paid forward in March and prior year arrears settled at intake.

Resolved each paying client number to its HMIS person through the migration crosswalk, then charged each payment to the project the applicant of record was enrolled in over the period that payment covers. The enrollment export is a history and the join fans out on the person alone, so it has to be closed with the date rather than by collapsing each client to one row: 4,138 lines worth USD 4,614,210.90 belong to other projects.

Recovered household identity from the coordinated entry rosters, which is the only source in the bundle carrying a household reference that survives a second presentation, since the HMIS household identifier is scoped to a single enrollment by the standard, then applied the operating year maximum once per household: 168 households reduced, USD 714,373.74 removed.
Certified figure: USD 6,468,921.99 across 1,829 households and 5,416 payment lines.

critical_components: The chart of accounts is effective dated, three cost centre code strings were retired and reissued to other providers on another funder's line inside the operating year, and a code therefore only identifies a funder together with the date the warrant cleared. Reading it as a flat code lookup either drops USD 763,594.33 of the Fund's own assistance or pulls in USD 786,763.42 that another funder paid, depending on which of the two rows the lookup happens to keep.

A disbursement month that comes back is not a copy of the month it replaces, because the reason it came back is that lines had been coded wrongly, so the load is an upsert on the warrant with the later delivery winning: 2,502 lines worth USD 2,710,202.01 are superseded.
A payment belongs to the period it covers rather than the date the warrant cleared, which leaves 1,192 lines worth USD 1,470,360.98 outside the measured window.

A payment is charged to the project the applicant of record was enrolled in over the period it covers, which is a temporal join against an enrollment history rather than a lookup against a per client state, and it leaves 4,138 lines worth USD 4,614,210.90 with other projects. This is the step that separates USD 6,468,921.99 from USD 4,043,014.35.

The operating year maximum applies once per household, and a household that presents again under a different applicant runs more than one client number in the fiscal system, so applying it at the client grain leaves USD 714,373.74 in the figure that the terms do not allow.
submission.recommendation: We certify USD 6,468,921.99 in support of the OY2028 renewal request. The figure rests on 1,829 households and 5,416 payment lines, out of 19,366 lines read. The number a competent pipeline produces without the last move is USD 4,043,014.35, which is 37.1 per cent short, and the three figures a solver passes through on the way there are USD 5,702,903.20 off a straight load, USD 5,147,184.61 once the re-delivered months are resolved, and USD 4,729,922.81 once payments are measured against the period they cover. Not the deputy director's position, which would hold the certification to the households the Fund is paying for on the prevention line today, and which is the single largest error available at USD 4,043,014.35. Not the reading that charges every payment to where the household first presented, which runs the other way at USD 8,190,892.05.

submission.objective_tag: Experiment and Causal Analysis (a causal claim from observational data
steps: Built money raised from everybody other than us by taking each grantee's contributed revenue schedule and removing the Foundation's own line. Nothing else on that schedule is earned revenue or a government contract, and the schedule totals tie to the contributions line of the annual financial summary to the dollar.

Collapsed the offer register, which is a fortnightly snapshot export and repeats every live offer, to one row per offer, and dropped the five offers the Foundation withdrew. That leaves 168 organisations offered the engagement across FY2021 to FY2025, and 48 offered it for FY2026 of which 42 have said yes. The provider agreement contracts 24 engagements, so 18 organisations that said yes get nothing.

Measured the raw picture first. Organisations that took the coaching raise a median of USD 2,095,472 against USD 1,595,864 for the rest in FY2025, a mean gap of USD 413,740 per organisation. The same gap is already there in FY2019 and FY2020, a median USD 184,776 before the programme existed, so it is not the coaching.

Applied the policy's measure: each organisation's own change in the year of its offer, net of the same change over the same two years for the organisations whose offer had not yet come due. Pooled across the five closed cohorts that is USD 166,521 per organisation offered.

Checked it against the one place the pack settles the causal question outright. Places were drawn by lot in every closed year because acceptances ran ahead of the contracted number, and 22 organisations accepted and were left on the waiting list. Drawn against waitlisted, which the draw randomises, is USD 221,606 per engagement. The finance committee's basis, every organisation that accepted against those that declined, is USD 428,228, and USD 239,563 of that sits between the organisations that accepted and were never drawn, who received nothing at all, and the organisations that declined. So 55.9 per cent of the gap finance uses is there before a session is delivered, at 10.2 standard errors from zero.

Put the measure onto a delivered engagement the way policy clause 4 sets out, by dividing by the 0.75 of offers that reached a place in the years the measure was taken on. Applied blind to the 24 places that gives USD 5,328,679, which misses the target.

Looked for what decides where a place is worth most. Split the offered organisations on budget, on age, on activity code, on state, on region and on grant vintage: not one of those cuts moves the measure, budget reaching a Welch t of 0.61 and the largest of the others under 1.9.

Split it instead on what the engagement actually does. The handbook describes a fixed individual giving sequence, a donor portfolio review, moves management for the households capable of a leadership gift, solicitation practice, a case statement and a stewardship plan, and coaches are instructed to decline institutional proposal work. Grantees name every source giving USD 5,000 or more, and the regional grantmakers directory says which of those names are grantmaking institutions, so counting the named sources that are not institutions gives each organisation's individual major gift pipeline. The distribution is bimodal with a hole in it: 2 named sources or fewer on one side, 22 or more on the other, in every year the pack covers.

Measured the policy's measure inside each side. USD 210,913 per offer above the split and USD 67,492 below it, at 10.55 and 4.00 standard errors from zero, the difference between them at 5.48. On a delivered engagement that is USD 281,218 against USD 89,990. A large organisation with no pipeline is moved USD 58,004, which is the point: size is not what the coaching acts on.

Allocated the 24 places. 28 of the 42 acceptors hold a pipeline, which is more than the places, so all 24 go to them and the commitment is USD 6,749,231.01. Spreading the places evenly across the acceptors instead would commit the board to USD 5,219,406, and placing them in the largest grantees lands in the same region, because budget is inert.

Built the interval the policy fixes, at 1.645 standard errors carried through the same arithmetic as the figure: USD 5,696,857.47 to USD 7,801,604.54, which is USD 5,700,000 to USD 7,800,000 to the nearest hundred thousand.
Recommendation: commit to USD 6,749,000, which clears the USD 6,000,000 target. ---

steps: Read the peak slotting standard. A carton-flow item gets a shelf face for peak only where the move reduces the direct pick hours its lines take over the quarter the face is released for, the desk's own basis is velocity first until the pool runs out, and a block's movement is reported as pick lines per labour hour, the closed quarter before the changeover against the weeks after it, as worked.

Build the picker-shift frame. Labour hours come from the LMS export at each booking's latest batch, posted only, and lines come from the confirm log with every line joined to the primary assignment in force on its work date, which also gives the kind of face the shift was slotted on. No shift mixes kinds of face.

Find the July block off the assignment history: 216 items whose primary face closed on a carton-flow location on 4 July and opened on a shelf location on 5 July, and nothing else changed kind of face that day.

Read the block the desk's way. Spring quarter 44.7 pick lines per labour hour against 55.5 in the weeks after, a gain of 24.3 percent. Shelf faces that did not move drifted -0.5 percent over the same weeks, so no period correction does any work. The number is right and the move worked. Stopping here files 288, or 200 once the pool is counted.

Split the block. Three shift-sharing groups rose 27.1 to 37.7 percent and three fell 15.1 to 23.0, and item by item, 144 rose and 72 fell with nothing in between. Every programme in the block carries a group of each sign, so the signs cannot be carried across by programme.

Find what separates them. Velocity, programme, case size and module each carry both kinds; eaches per line off the confirm log carries the split completely, and the block's own gap (1.28 to 3.48) fixes the boundary at 2.38.

Measure that property on the right quarter. An item's eaches per line is how the quarter orders it, and the folder holds one closed peak, the 2025 trading weeks. On those lines 66 of the requested items sit below the boundary; on the spring's lines 138 do. The flip runs both ways: 30 items are bought singly only at peak and earn a face, and 102 that look like single pickers in the spring go out as assortments at peak and lose one.

Check the read that points the other way. Shelf faces against carton-flow faces in the spring quarter, July block aside, run 39.7 against 47.9 lines an hour on singles and 39.8 against 32.8 on multi-unit lines, which would say move the multi-unit items. But on the same shelf faces in the same weeks the moved singles ran 64.9 lines an hour against the residents' 39.6 and the moved multi items 27.3 against 39.5, so the shelf-resident ranges are different items with their own handling.

Count and check the pool. 66 items move (Arborway 36 of 66, Castello 30 of 132, Dunmore 0 of 72, Lorimer 0 of 18) against 200 spare active shelf faces with no assignment of any type in force on 4 October, so the pool does not bind.
Recommendation: move 66 items on the shutdown, the ones the peak quarter buys as singles.

steps: Settled the grain of the member position before building anything, because the charter's condition names a quantity that only exists at one of two grains and the choice cannot be deferred to the end. Held each award's position separately rather than summing them per member. Eight members were carrying a positive balance on some awards while holding grantor cash on others at the same date, and collapsing them to one pot per member drops three of the eight out of the qualifying set without adding any member back.

Settled which record wins where the three sources disagree. Joined the award register to the expenditure reports and the remittance register on `award_id`, kept only the highest version of each award, service month and cost category, because the dictionary says later versions supersede and summing across them double counts, which affects 86 restated award months, and summed the remittance register whole, because each of the 34 voided warrants carries a reversal that cancels it. That leaves 25,877 report rows and 2,388 remittance rows in play.
Built cumulative cost and cumulative cash received for each award, to each month end from the opening of the extract through 30 June 2025.

Verified the conformed table against the audited statements before using it, which is what turns step 1 from a preference into the only available construction. Reported grants and contracts receivable equals the sum of the positive award positions at the close, and reported refundable advances equals the sum of the negative ones, for all twenty-four members. For the sixteen members reporting a refundable advance, no netted figure reproduces the reported one, so the statements themselves say the positions are held apart.

Took each member's own liquid resources from the monthly liquidity certificates, as cash plus short-term investments, less the restricted portion of cash, less the grantor cash carried at the award grain from step 3. The certificates carry no receivable and no grantor balance, so the conformed table is the only route to that deduction.

Applied charter 2.2 across the twelve month ends of PY2025. Eight of twenty-four members had a positive unfunded operating position at some month end. Six of the eight peak at 31 October 2024 and two peak at 31 December 2024, which is where the state's contract execution cycle and the behavioural health division's own settlement rhythm put them.
Applied charter 3.1. The eight advance limits sum to $6,912,427.09.
Applied charter 4.1 and rounded up to $6,925,000.

critical_components: **The grain the position is built at, and the positive tail it produces.** What an award still owes cannot go below zero, so what a member is owed is the sum over its awards of each award's own unpaid cost, and an award that has been paid ahead of its own cost has not paid for any other award's cost. Held award by award the position peaks between $171,395 and $2,483,408 over the eight members, and the audited receivable line is the sum of exactly these positive positions at each member's close, which is what says the charter's condition is written against this grain rather than against a member-level net.

**The negative tail, which is the grantor cash each member holds against cost it has not yet incurred**, read at the same grain and taken out of the member's own resources. Sixteen of the twenty-four were holding some at their fiscal close, the liquidity certificates carry no such balance so the rebuilt award positions are the only route to it, and the audited refundable advances line is the sum of exactly these negative positions.

**The set of members whose unfunded operating position is positive at any month end of the completed programme year**, which is eight of twenty-four, and is not a subset of the annual screen's four member watch list.
**Each member's advance limit** at one twelfth of its total expenses as most recently audited, which over the eight sums to $6,912,427.09 before rounding.
submission.recommendation: The Trust should obligate **$6,925,000** to the Member Working Capital Line for programme year 2027. That is the sum of the advance limits of the eight members the Line stands behind, $6,912,427.09, rounded up to the charter's twenty-five thousand dollar increment. The eight are PCM-107, PCM-110, PCM-113, PCM-122, PCM-125, PCM-131, PCM-137 and PCM-170, out of a membership of twenty-four. Not $1,750,000, which is what the four members on the annual screen's watch list come to. Not $1,125,000, which is what the charter's own condition comes to if you read it off the audited statements at each member's fiscal close. Not $2,900,000, which is what it comes to if you rebuild the position month by month but let each member's awards settle against each other. The last of those is the one to beat, and the answer is 2.39 times it.

steps: Built the monthly claim rate per 1,000 units shipped from the order lines and the claims register, dropping intakes that carry a `superseded_by` reference: a trailing twelve-month rate of 20.7 to February 2026, then 35.5 in March and 35.3 in April, with July at 23.7 still above the two-year rate, so the problem is live at the pull, and intake-to-ship lags confirm the register is complete (over 98 percent of claims file within 90 days).

Replayed the stock rotation rule the operations manual files, oldest receipt first within each SKU and site over CURRENT ASN revisions, and back-tested it against the lot trace drills. The only lot-coded postings in the history are the 2024 CAPA's year-end withdrawal, and only relieving the lot each posting names reproduces the scans, 513 of 513 audited picks against 486 for the plain queue-order treatment.

Decoded press weeks off the carton lot code and put the rise on lots pressed in ISO weeks 2549 to 2552, 132 claims per 1,000 against 20, explaining the rise on its own, then carried the replay to the pull and found the cohort still flowing: shipments through 2026-08-12 and 1,965 units on the racks, so containment reads as the urgent, causal, biggest-number pick, about 221 claims priced against the pile.
Cut the window by channel for the driver's shipments: palletized dealer volume 38.6 per 1,000 against 27.1 for all other shipments, a 1.4 multiple.

Joined the item master's carton weights to the order lines, rebuilt each pallet stack heaviest at the base as the manual's build standard states, and scored every carton by the weight stacked above it: ex-cohort window rates run 13.9, 19.3, 26.3, and 64.5 per 1,000 across the bands, stacked 36.0 against single-carton 14.2, and the gradient holds on will-call pallets no carrier touches (32.6 stacked will-call against 31.7 stacked LTL over 2025), so the crush is built at pack-out.

Asked what the funded window actually contains for each programme. The reserve review convenes 3 September (the thread fixes the date) and the manual's section 6 costs a programme on the claims it avoids on the units shipped inside the funded period, so the containment's reach is not the pile, it is the slice of the pile that ships in September through November.

Projected each cohort-holding sku-site queue forward under the filed rotation rule, with demand read five ways (trailing four weeks, trailing twelve weeks, the September plan scaled to sku shares, and 30 percent slower and faster): 621 to 796 units ship inside the window, 70 to 89 claims, the rest shipping before the programme can exist or trailing out after November (about 1,106 units), and the pile figure itself is invariant to the posting-treatment fork, so no replay convention moves the scope.

Costed the five programmes on the filed basis over the funded quarter: pallet build about 170 (13,080 planned dealer units, three fifths stacked, at the window's own stack effect), containment at most 89, carrier revert about 82 even crediting the intake coding that will-call parity refutes, liner about 24 (12 percent tail at 26.6 against 18.8), and peak staffing nothing once stacked weight is held (promo weeks file like their shoulder weeks within every band).
Recommendation: fund the pack-out and pallet-build QA programme at both DCs.

steps: Read the ordinance: a cap of 15, a filed floor of 17,750 USD, eligibility on the fiscal year last closed, certification on the remittances for the months the change moves, and the two remittance calendars.

Derived the moved months from the calendars: April and May, and nothing else, since June is a following-year receipt on either schedule.

Built the eligible pool: 102 accounts registered quarterly at the close of FY2026 with FY2026 liability at or above the floor. Every reading of the registered class (the FY2026 rows, the class at June 2026, the last class in the extract) selects the same 102.
Measured behaviour from received dates: 52 of the 102 settle April and May on the monthly due dates despite their quarterly registration, so a placement moves nothing for them.

Noticed the register itself moves: the class column flips through the extract, 236 times, at dates that are quarter starts scattered across the years rather than any single event beyond the filed 1 July 2025 reclassification.

Recovered the rule behind the movement by back-testing candidate rules against every observed class sample: reviews at each account's registration anniversary, a two-year test against the floor, effect from the next quarter start. Zero contradictions in 58,374 samples; every rival contradicts the ledger at least 17 times.

Projected each eligible account's registered class through FY2027 from closed facts: the 20 accounts with FY2025 and FY2026 both at or above the floor and anniversaries before April are moved to monthly remittance by the register itself before the tranche's months fall due, so a placement brings forward nothing for them either.

Took the settled outcomes: the 2025 signup cohort has **200 accounts whose tier log carries a guided to self_serve change on or before the extract date**, and the register file carries every class occurrence underneath them, so any candidate rule can be run forward and scored to the day.

Ran the account grain candidates first. Total registers closed, and registers per rostered coach, both fitted with a single threshold: **best mean absolute errors of 173.2 and 103.9 days**, and in each case a flat loss curve, so neither pins a threshold and neither pins a block size.

Moved to coach grain and tried registers per coach with the slowest coach binding: **94.9 days**, still flat across 52 to 84. Three pairs of settled accounts show why. CD-042469 and CD-042472 are the same discipline, the same district, the same plan, the same signup date, four coaches each, 1,833 against 1,845 registers over the extract window, and every individual coach's register count matches within 1.91 per cent. Counted **separate days taught** rather than classes taken. The coach who separates those twins runs six classes on one day a week where her opposite number runs one class on each of six days, so they close the same registers and bank six times the days. **46 separate days per coach, with the slowest coach on the roster binding, reproduces all 200 settled changes to the day, and no other integer between 10 and 120 reproduces more than 2 of them, 45 and 47 included.**

That figure ties to the guided account count the Brackenhall capacity schedule reports at the August month end, and the platform's own tier change log independently names the same 370.

**The rule that moves an account off guided support is a count of separate teaching days per coach, and 46 is the number.** An account leaves guided support on the first day its school teaches on which every coach then on its roster has taken classes on at least 46 separate days. Recovered against the 200 handovers already settled in the 2025 signup cohort, 46 reproduces all 200 to the day. 45 and 47 each reproduce 2 of the 200.

**Each rostered coach's count of separate teaching days, carried forward past the extract.** For every account in the book, and for every coach on its roster at the relevant date, the number of distinct dates that coach has taken at least one class on, running through the closed history and on into the published autumn timetable. There are **1,406** such coaches across the book and **939** of them reach 46 separate days by the term close. The account's clock is the slowest of its own coaches, and coaches who join or leave are counted at their roster dates.

**Carrying the rule through the published autumn timetable clears 146.** Each account's autumn term work is read rather than projected, because the timetable is built and locked during enrolment and every one of the 159,191 autumn occurrences in the register file carries a scheduled_on before the extract date. Running each roster forward to 18 December 2026 gives 146 accounts clearing inside the term and 224 still on guided support at the close.

steps: Read the four telemetry files, found every maximal span of return air above the 8.0 ceiling the manual qualifies vehicles to, and kept the spans that outlast the 20 minute alert rule the vehicle register sets: 48 qualifying deviations in the reference period. Every span in the archive is either 10 minutes or less or 40 minutes or more, so any cut between 11 and 39 minutes selects the same 48, and the rule is not a convention call.

Joined the manifests to the proof of delivery times and worked out, for each deviation, which consignments had not yet been handed over when the span started. That set reproduces the QA dispositions on all 48 investigations, and it totals 2,032 packs against the 2,032 the ledger credits to vehicle temperature losses.
Checked the two rival readings on the same 48. Writing off everything on the run reproduces 0 of

Writing off only the drop being made reproduces 0 of 48. Reading the split by planned stop order rather than by delivery time reproduces all 48, so those two readings converge and the choice between them does not matter.

Separated the spring rise. Of 3,147 packs of temperature write-off on live credit lines, 1,115 arose in the Haydock cold store, all of them inside the pack A failure the maintenance register dates from 9 February to the replacement on 21 April and the re-qualification on 24 April. That is 35.4 per cent, it is resolved, and it is not a vehicle loss.

Cleared the ledger. A block of the spring cold store credits went out without batch references, was withdrawn and re-raised in May, and 694 packs sit on the withdrawn lines. Summing the ledger as it stands counts those twice.

Measured the hazard. The 48 deviations run at 1.35 per 1,000 calls, and per-call the rate agrees across the two run types at 1.38 and 0.99, while per run it splits 3.7 to 1 and per hour 7 to 1, so the call is what generates a deviation and not the run or the hour. Every qualifying onset sits 5 to 9 minutes after a proof of delivery stamp, which is the door opening the compartment fails to recover from. Per vehicle the counts are consistent with one fleet rate, chi-square 10.48 on 14 degrees of freedom.

Built the exposure quantity on both sides. Reference period: 35,676 calls, 506,822 packs, 1,509,136 pack-legs. Published plan: 9,027 calls, 126,567 packs, 1,055,638 pack-legs. The plan carries 0.999 of a reference quarter's volume to the same customers and 2.80 times the pack-legs.

Applied the per-call hazard to the plan's pack-legs: 1,420.3 packs. Cross-checked by scaling the observed 2,032 packs by the pack-leg ratio, which gives 1,421.4, a difference of 0.076 per cent and the same committed figure.
Recommendation: commit 1,420 packs.

steps: Read the amendment letter and the FY2027 guarantee schedule: from November 2 the per-item floors rise (Greek cups 26 to 28 days, cottage 14 to 16, kefir 16 to 17, smoothies 21 to 24, dips 50 to 60), product with code life not less than the guarantee conforms, non-conforming product is refused instead of drawing the 5 percent per-case allowance, and a 98.5 percent vendor line-acceptance floor is measured over P1 to P6.

Settled dollars by family: kefir 151,450, cottage 45,706, smoothies 1,941, Greek cups 0, dips 0.

Replayed the FY2027 floors against the historical case book as a first cut: cottage cheese leads, kefir second, Greek cups and dips zero, but the replay runs on the outgoing plan's age masses and the September wheel changes them.

Established how lots are dated, from the lot record rather than from any document. Grouping the offset (printed life less sell-by minus pack) by filler line returns a single value of zero on every line except Owatonna P2-L2, which returns two values, seven and eight. A single per-line constant therefore cannot reproduce the record. Grouping P2-L2's lots by production week shows why: each cycle's lots share one lot-code julian day while filling on two different days, so the code date belongs to the cycle's vat and each block loses the days it sat. Solving for the vat lead gives seven days as the unique value reproducing every lot code in the file.

Built the forward stock position from the August 21 snapshot plus in-transit lots plus every planned wheel run, dating each planned L2 lot from its own cycle's vat, and served the FY2027 standing grid first-expired-first-out with the lane master's fixed transits. critical_components: The printed sell-by on a lot runs from the vat date its lot code carries, not from the fill date, and on Owatonna P2-L2 one vat feeds a whole production cycle. So a P2-L2 lot's code life at receipt is short of fill-plus-printed-life by however many days it sat before its own fill, which is seven days for the block that opens the cycle and eight for the block that follows it. The lot record settles this: all 88 lots P2-L2 has ever filled carry one of exactly two offsets, never a single constant, while every other line carries zero.

The vat lead is recoverable exactly and is seven days. It is the unique value under which every one of the 4,462 shipped lot codes equals its lot's vat day, and the four historical L2 cycles each show one lot-code day shared across two different fill days, which is what refutes the natural reading that a lot code carries its fill date.

The P1 to P6 position is built forward from the filed anchors (the September to April production wheel, the accepted FY2027 standing grid, the August 21 JCS inventory, the lot record, first-expired-first-out serving), with each planned L2 lot dated from its own cycle's vat. The wheel alternates which block opens each L2 cycle, so Greek cups take the seven-day offset in half the cycles and the eight-day offset in the others.

Scored at the settlement grain the amended terms impose (a line below guarantee is refused in full, on its oldest case, and a line at exactly the guarantee conforms), the committed book projects 157 refused lines and 516,267 dollars, of which Greek cups carry 144 lines and 443,449 dollars.
submission.recommendation: We should commit to 516,267 dollars of refusal exposure for the first Bluestem compliance review window, periods P1 to P6, November 2, 2026 through May 2, 2027. That is 157 refused lines out of the 3,068 committed order lines, and projected vendor line acceptance of 94.9 percent against the 98.5 percent program floor. Greek cups carry 443,449 dollars of it, 85.9 percent, on 144 of their 780 lines; smoothie drinks 57,566, kefir 15,252, cottage cheese and dips nothing. Not 72,818 dollars, which is what the commitment comes to if every planned lot is dated at its fill date plus the printed life on the item master. Not 303,650 dollars, and not 572,034 dollars, which are what it comes to under the two flat per-line offsets the lot record shows. Each of those is a defensible reading of a correct file, and each one misses the commitment by between 11 and 86 percent.

submission.domain_tag: Nonprofit and grant-making (giving strategy and program funding).
submission.objective_tag: Descriptive and distribution analysis (how a population is composed).
steps: Read the guidelines. The appropriation is the most the cycle could award, being the schedule amount for every place it could fill, and a place is filled by making a grant to an eligible organization, so the appropriation is bounded by the organizations the line is still allowed to fund as well as by the places it carries.

Assemble every return on file from the Service's published extracts. The Service publishes the long form and the short form as separate annual archives, and the shipped pack carries both for filing years 2019 to 2023, so the panel is 17,841 long-form returns and 9,944 short-form returns, 27,785 in all. The Service's own column names differ between the two forms and between releases, so each field is resolved by the names it is published under rather than by assuming one, and reading a single set of names silently drops a third of the returns.

Take each organization's most recent return, apply the guidelines' recency test, and run the seven eligibility tests against the Master File. The Cycle 2025 screen is 457 organizations. Deduplicating by latest fiscal period and deduplicating by newest release select the same 457 organizations and the same bands, so that convention does not move the figure.

Build the recipient history and remove it. The award register carries 350 executed agreements, the predecessor award list carries 100 grants with the identifier in a different shape, and the application log carries 364 award decisions against the register's 350, so 14 organizations were offered a grant and never executed an agreement and guidelines 6 treats each of them as having held one.
Count what is left, band by band: 100 organizations in Band 1, 65 in Band 2 and 7 in Band 3.

Compare with the places. Bands 1 and 2 are far above their limits, so they fill 12 and 22 places and are appropriated in full. Band 3 carries 36 places and has 7 organizations left, so 29 of its places cannot be filled.
Price it against the schedule: 180,000 plus 660,000 plus 630,000, giving **1,470,000 dollars** for 41 grants.

Check it against the closed record. The line filled all 70 of its places in every one of the five closed cycles, so each awarded 4,080,000 dollars, and the fall is entirely the population running out rather than any change in the schedule or the places.

critical_components: The population of Kentucky organizations that satisfy the guidelines' seven eligibility tests at the Cycle 2025 screen is built from every return on file, which means both published extract families across all five releases, giving 27,785 returns for 6,559 organizations and a screen of 457 organizations.

The recipient history that is removed from that screen has three parts, being the 350 executed Organizational Strengthening Grants, the 100 grants under the 2016 to 2019 Capacity Grants programme, and the 14 organizations that were offered a grant and never executed an agreement, which guidelines 6 treats as having held one.
The eligible and never funded population is 100 organizations in Band 1, 65 in Band 2 and 7 in Band 3.
The cycle carries 12 places in Band 1, 22 in Band 2 and 36 in Band 3, so Bands 1 and 2 can fill every place they carry and Band 3 can fill 7 of its 36.
The appropriation is the schedule amount for every place the cycle could fill, which is 12 times 15,000 plus 22 times 30,000 plus 7 times 90,000, or 1,470,000 dollars.
submission.recommendation: The Board should approve an appropriation of **1,470,000 US dollars** for the Cycle 2025 Organizational Strengthening Grant line. That provides for 41 grants, being 12 in Band 1 at 15,000 dollars, 22 in Band 2 at 30,000 dollars and 7 in Band 3 at 90,000 dollars, and it is 64 per cent below the 4,080,000 dollars the line awarded in Cycle 2024 and in each of the four cycles before it. Not 4,080,000, which is what the line has awarded in every closed cycle and what carrying the places forward gives. Not 1,065,000, which is what the screen returns if the population is built from the long-form returns alone. Not 2,370,000, which is what it returns if the organizations that were offered a grant and never executed an agreement are left in the pool, and not 2,010,000, which is what it returns if the filing-recency test is not applied.

steps: Put the two houses on one schema. Valley City writes settlement bushels; the Litchville station runs older software, writes fixed-width records with moisture and the other grade factors in tenths and no decimal point, and computes no settlement bushels at all, so they come off its net pounds under the posted schedule. That is 14,588 house tickets and 4,775 station receipts.

Take the house's transfer tickets out of the receipts. 1,693 of the Valley City tickets carry the origin code the field reference explains as a Company haul of grain the station had already taken in, each one naming the station receipt it came from, and they carry 1,078,343.70 bushels that the Company did not buy from anybody a second time. Counting them is worth $4,108,562.58 on the run.

Scope the wind-up to the programme the Board actually closed. steps: **Read the charter.** Part 2 says the transfer is a carried component plus a new component, Part 2.2 holds the carried side to the weeks that remain in each benefit year and fall inside the period, Part 2.3 puts the new side on separations dated inside the period, Part 2.4 says the separations a notice reports are those of the workers employed at the establishment it names, and Part 3 carries the entitlement arithmetic. Part 1.3 fixes the certification to the notices on file at the December date.

**Scope the register.** Nine notices carry separations into the period. The phase schedule, not the register header, holds the dates, and it comes in two date formats because it is keyed off the filed forms. Prorating each notice to its in-period phases gives 2,545 positions against 3,216 on the notices as a whole, and one superseded row drops out.

**Take each notice's population where the notice points.** The register names an account and a worksite; the worksite employment report maps that worksite to a reporting unit; the wage records are filed by reporting unit. Three of the nine notices sit at accounts that run more than one reporting unit, and those three carry 1,916 of the 2,545 in-period positions. Taken at the reporting unit, the nine populations carry $20,366,486 of entitlement. Taken at the account, they carry $34,908,996.

**Compute entitlement per Part 3 on the base period that applies.** Every in-period phase falls in the first quarter of 2027, so every one of these benefit years draws on 2025Q4 through 2026Q3, which the extract carries in full. 2,387 of the 3,216 qualify. At the three multi-unit sites and the Fenwick contact floor the qualifying share runs 67.1 to 70.6 per cent, and among those who do qualify a large block is held by the wage test rather than by the 26 week test, so the entitlement is short at both ends.

**Recover the conversion from the settled cohorts.** Charter 2.6 strikes the rate on the settled cohorts taken together, as established benefit years per monetarily eligible worker, so the 21 of them give 5,013 over 6,366, or 0.787465. Applied to each notice's own entitlement, that rule reproduces all 21 settled cohorts within 7.3 per cent and 3.2 per cent on average. The obligation each noticed position has carried, $10,349, ties the settled total by construction and misses individual cohorts badly: 3 of 21 by 25 per cent or more, 11 of 21 by 15 per cent or more, and the worst by 204 per cent.

**Hold each new benefit year to the weeks it has inside the period.** Applying the rate to the whole entitlement of the eligible population gives $13,285,586, and that figure cannot reproduce a single settled period: rebuilt that way, the four settled halves come out 19.4 to 58.1 per cent above what the Council actually certified, and the Desk's error goes from 2.6 per cent to 25.6 per cent. Rebuilt with each benefit year held to the compensable weeks it can be drawn before its period closes, every settled half ties within 3.1 per cent. The period's separations run from 5 February to 31 March 2027, so the nine cohorts have between 13 and 21 weeks, and $14,573,109 of the $20,366,486 the population carries survives that hold.
**New obligation: $9,306,641**, or $3,657 a position, against the $10,349 a position the settled record has carried.

**Carried obligation: $13,541,252.** 2026 opened three large cohorts whose benefit years run out inside the first half of 2027, so a good part of the unexhausted balance cannot be drawn before it lapses. Held to the weeks that remain, the carried side is $13,541,252 against $16,396,161 unheld.

steps: Rebuilt the settled attainments from the assessment record, because the programme and credential detail behind a settlement is an Office working paper and is not in the extract set, so the payment summary is the only record to check against. A pass counts when the student is reported at concentrator status in that programme of study that year, the credential is on that year's approved list for that programme, and it is the student's earliest recorded pass of it. That reading reproduces every settled district and program year; every rival misses.

Dated each agreement to the program year it was executed in. A program year runs 1 August to 31 July and is named for the year it opens, so a board that adopted in February 2025 adopted in PY2024-25, not PY2025-26.

Recovered the run length from the payment summary. Nothing states how long an agreement runs, so I ran each candidate forward: three program years counted from the year of execution reproduces every settled district-year and no other run length does. Ninety-six districts are covered for PY2027-28.

Counted concentrators rather than roster rows. Terms 2.1 says a student is one concentrator however many programmes the district reports them in, and the rosters carry a row per programme, so PY2027-28 is 31,305 rows for 23,832 concentrators, 31.4 per cent apart.

submission.domain_tag: Product Analytics, monetization and subscriptions (seat based B2B billing).
submission.objective_tag: Data Extraction and Conformation (ETL / Pipeline Build).
steps: Took the closing month of the seat ledger, which is the record of what was billable under policy BP-4 1.1, and summed billable seats across the 1,060 lines open at 31 December 2025: 41,820 seats.

Checked that count against the payment processor's December remittance rather than against the event feed, because the remittance is the record of what was actually billed. It settles 41,820 seats for USD 1,313,782.00 and it ties line for line, not merely in total, so the base is not adjusted.

Examined the three structures that make the ledger count look inflated against a feed derived count, and found each one legitimate and documented. 210 lines carry 7,530 seats on accounts that also hold an earlier lapsed line, which BP-4 2.1 makes separate subscriptions. 150 lines carry 5,460 seats in the region whose provisioning service was retired on 1 August 2025, whose feed stopped while billing continued. 4,380 seats are delegated administrator seats, billable since 1 April 2025 under BP-4 4.2.

Read what a plan is built on. BP-4 1.3 says a plan for a period carries the closing billable base of the period before it together with every change taking effect inside the period, so the question is not what was billable in December, it is what the quarter will carry.
Read the contract book on effective date rather than on signature, per BP-4 5.1, which puts 2,140 seats inside 2026 Q1 and leaves 1,193 seats on 28 notes outside it.

Read the channel agreement register. MA-4101 runs to 31 December 2025 with no successor agreement recorded against it, the other three live agreements run to 30 June 2026, 31 December 2026 and 31 March 2027, and every one of the six prior agreements in the register's history was succeeded by a successor recorded by the day its term fell due.

Resolved that agreement's schedule as it stands at the close. The crosswalk is the record of the schedule in force under clause 4.1 of the standard terms, one row per partner account code per spell, and 178 spells against MA-4101 are open at the close, carrying 9,187 seats in the partner return. The return also still carries 14 codes at 2,150 seats whose spells closed on 14 December, filed by Nordhaven on 8 December before that block of accounts moved to Sundberg; the same accounts appear in force under new MA-4103 codes at close counts, so counting the closed spells books the block twice and against the wrong agreement.

Applied clause 9.2 of the standard terms to the 178 accounts. On expiry each account continues on its own subscription line with its seats billed to the account from the day after. 152 of the accounts each hold exactly one open line, and their 7,260 seats come direct on 1 January. The other 26 hold only lapsed lines: BP-4 2.1 says a lapsed line is not reopened and a new line takes a signed order, the contract schedule carries no order for any of them, and BP-4 1.1 counts billable seats per subscription line, so their 1,927 seats enter no line inside the quarter. The channel's own settled history says the same thing: all 16 prior schedule exits whose account held an open line stepped that line in the month after the spell closed, and none of the 6 exits without one landed a seat until a new order was signed months later, two of which did exactly that.
Committed count: 41,820 plus 2,140 plus 7,260 is 51,220 seats.

steps: Parsed the mainframe extract on both of its record layouts (the oil field widened from seven to eight characters at the 2025-01 block and every field after it moves one column right) and netted the 2,685 adjustment records through the trailing sign overpunch, which gives 31,806,770 barrels for 2024 and 2025 together.

Took the portal export down to one row per filed number and production month, keeping the highest version received at or before the cut of 5 p.m. central on 15 August 2028 and dropping the filings that were returned to the operator. A filing still in review at the cut is certified as filed, so the review status stays in.

Resolved every filing to the property through the well master on the ten digit number, because operators re-file a completion under the event number the Commission assigns it and an exact join on the fourteen digit number silently drops those rows. Filings whose well is not on the district master are referred, not certified, which is 60 rows.

Collapsed the resolved filings to one per well and production month, keeping the one received last. This has to run after the resolve and not before it, because the two filings of a re-entered completion carry two different fourteen digit numbers and are two separate rows at the grain the portal export is written at. Skipping it certifies 3,055,313.

Built the qualifying period, being 2026-07 to 2027-06, as the union of the two systems with the portal as the record of any month both hold, which matters because the mainframe ran to 2027-03 and the portal opened in 2026-10.

Recovered the divisor from the determination register rather than assuming it. The register carries 534 filed determinations for certification years 2026 and 2027 with the average each one was made on to three decimal places, and the average over the wells completed and unplugged through the period reproduces every one of them. Dividing by the wells that filed production gets 83 of the 534 wrong and runs 16.8 per cent high on the register's own total, and dividing by every well on the master gets 77 wrong and runs 16.3 per cent low.
Determined certification year 2028 on that basis: 109 of the 267 properties average under 15.0 barrels a day per well over the qualifying period, and their production is not taxable.

critical_components: Certification year 2028 has to be determined on its own qualifying period, being the twelve production months to 30 June 2027. Nothing on file determines it. The determination register closes at certification year 2027, the property register carries no determination at all, and the standard does not carry a determination beyond the year it was made for.

The qualifying average is taken over the wells the operator holds completed and unplugged through the period, read as of each month of it, which is the only divisor that reproduces all 534 filed determinations in the register for the two closed years.

The quarter's filings are the two reporting systems unioned with the portal standing as the record of any month both of them hold, resolved to the well on the ten digit number rather than to the number as filed, and including the filings still in review at the cut.

The certification is built at one filing per well and production month. Resolving the filed number to the well is what makes that binding, because a completion re-entered inside the quarter is filed a second time under the event number the Commission assigns it, and the two filings only land on the same well once the resolve has been done. 201 quarter filings on 67 wells arrive that way and they carry 527,235 barrels.

steps: Repaired the extract. The 2026 meter is a re-cut that writes its billing month in that team's own convention, and across the three years the meter carries 15,001 rows that re-state a branch, month and product combination a batch emission already carried. At the documented grain it holds 2,733,678 completed reports, and that figure ties to the reports the standing invoices bill in every one of the ten closed quarters, to the report.

Rebuilt every closed invoice from the published schedule in force in its own month. 836 of the 38,786 closed invoice events carry an amount the schedule does not reproduce, and every one of them is an invoice that was withdrawn. Where a replacement was raised it comes in $1,062,903.90 below the invoice it replaced, and 254 withdrawn invoices were never raised again. The closed record stands at $9,075,677.48 after the $116,014.12 of credits, rebills and write-offs raised against it.

Fixed the population. The branch register carries 3,177 branches and the billing runs know of 23 more that have closed and come off it. The commitment is struck over the 3,177, and 596 of them carry no contracted volume in the quarter and bill their base charge all the same.

Read the plan of record. Terms 4.2 says the filing in force at the quarter's open is the plan, taken account by account, and for 2027Q3 there is one filing, filed 19 June, contracting 1,482,424 reports. 562,547 of those reports sit in months before their branch is activated, and terms 1.4 says a request the platform does not accept is not made.

Served the quarter against Rowan's own capacity. An account's monthly ceiling is its provisioned seat balance times the 260 reports a seat serves, counting only the EFFECTIVE provisioning rows, drawn in the order the plan files the account's branches, with unserved demand carried to the next month. That serves 783,009 reports.

Found the constraint the seat model cannot see. Every screening product is ordered from an upstream source, several products share a source, `source_throughput.csv` states what each source completes a month across the whole platform, and how the platform draws when a month's orders exceed that access is recorded rather than stated: `order_returns.csv` carries the orders the sources returned unfilled, demand in a constrained cell is the meter plus the returns, and of the candidate draw disciplines exactly one reproduces the returns, products in the filed sequence, the marginal product pro rata across the branches ordering it and rounded down, the leftover searches one per branch in the plan's filed order and by branch identifier on a tie. Fitted to the 3,581 constrained cells it misses none, and the nearest rival misses 674. In the closed record the collection and laboratory network completed exactly 19,500 searches a month in July and August 2026 and the registry access network exactly 14,800, each of them its own filed quota to the search, so the constraint is real and is already operating. Applied to the summer book it binds in ten source months and cuts 194,035 reports, so the quarter completes 588,974 and carries 136,868 past the quarter end.

Priced it on the schedule in force. Terms 4.3 strikes the commitment on the entitlement schedule in force at the quarter's open, which is R5 from 1 July 2027, not the R4 the whole closed record prices under. The quarter bills $3,111,552.25, of which $1,457,646.25 is above the allowance, September is the largest month at $1,196,585.05 and 38.46 per cent, and the West carries the largest regional share at $622,337.65.
Recommendation: file $3,111,552.25.

critical_components: A report needs both a seat and an upstream search. Seats are Rowan's own capacity and are provisioned to each account, but every screening product is ordered from a source that completes a fixed number of searches a month across the whole platform, so the binding constraint sits on a grouping the account partition never forms.
The seat model alone would serve 783,009 reports in the quarter. The source quotas cut 194,035 of them, binding in ten source months, and the quarter completes 588,974.

The quarter opens under schedule revision R5, which takes force on 1 July 2027, while every closed month in the record prices under R4, so a pricing function calibrated on the closed record is calibrated on the wrong schedule.

Priced branch by branch and calendar month by calendar month under the schedule in force, over the 3,177 branches the register carries, the quarter bills $3,111,552.25, of which September carries $1,196,585.05 and 38.46 per cent.
submission.recommendation: We should file **$3,111,552.25** as the committed revenue for the quarter that opened on 1 July 2027. Of that figure $1,653,906.00 is base charge and $1,457,646.25 is charged above the included allowance on 247,156 reports. Not $3,951,912.75, which is what the platform's own seat capacity allows and sits 27.01 per cent high, because Rowan does not produce verification reports, it orders searches from upstream sources, and those sources cannot supply the summer book. Not $4,873,011.33, which is the revenue desk's blended rate of $3.287191 a report applied to the contracted volume, 56.6 per cent high. Not $6,445,076.30, which is the plan of record priced straight off the schedule as filed. Not $3,495,601.00, which reads one seat balance for the whole quarter. Not $2,119,017.60, which prices the quarter on the schedule the closed months are priced under, 31.90 per cent low. And not $2,754,5

steps: Resolved the population Chapter 7.4 asks for. Surrenders and revocations come out, permits whose term ends before 1 July 2029 with no renewal application on file come out, permits whose term ends before that day with a timely renewal application stay in, and construction permits stay in only where they authorise operation to begin on or before the day. That leaves 662 operations from a register of 700.

Netted the permit conditions marked federally enforceable, both the plant-wide hour caps written against ALL and the unit-level throughput caps, and left the state-only conditions out because 7.2(c) says they do not limit the potential.

Constituted the sources at the unit. Chapter 7.2(f) makes a source the whole of the stationary activities on contiguous or adjacent property under one control in one industrial group, and an activity is an emission unit, so the grouping key is the ultimate controller, the surveyed section the unit's own parcel sits in, and the two-digit code on the permit that authorises it. The operation register carries a correspondence address and no parcel, so the only place of record for an activity is the parcel on its own row. That gives 644 sources.

Walked the equity holdings up to an ultimate controller, taking a holding as control only above fifty per cent and chaining it through intermediates the holder itself controls, which is what separates a two-hop majority from a pair of forty-five per cent stakes. Built the hazardous potentials. Classified each source on the higher of its criteria and its hazardous readings, took the Class A sources, summed each one's potential over the five assessable pollutants with each pollutant capped at 125 tons, priced it at 42 dollars and 50 cents a ton and rounded each source's fee down to the dollar as 7.6(e) directs. steps: Built the statistical record from the extracts: kept the latest accepted version of each declaration, collapsed repeated transmissions to one copy per declaration line, restricted to customs procedure 10 per the standard's schedule, took the statistical month from the acceptance date, converted JAS-scale quantities to cubic metres at 0.906, and added the contingency-channel submissions the manifest says are never merged into extracts. That is 2,188,677 line records in the main files plus 1,567 contingency rows.

Replicated the July screen from the record and it ties the shipped file to the digit: dairy z -7.17 (value -33.6 per cent year on year), fruit -4.38 (-27.5), meat -3.07 (-10.0), and chapter 22 fourth at -2.00 (-4.0), with nothing else beyond 1.6.

Tested the dairy fall against the auction index and the activity side: unit values track the published index slide while the chapter's like-for-like movement is -0.9 per cent, so the movement is a price development and out of annex scope under the standard.

Tested the fruit fall against the season: monthly July value is far down but the twelve-month like-for-like movement is +2.2 per cent, and the monthly profile shows the harvest peaking and clearing weeks earlier than prior years, so the July reading is timing, not lost activity.

Ran the value track to its end: with both loud movers explained, no remaining chapter's value movement stands out against its own history (meat's -10.0 per cent July reading sits inside its record of irregular processing dips), so the value basis files a nil return. That result is what forced the question of which basis the annex actually turns on.

Back-tested candidate bases against the register's 17 filed dispositions: the matched like-for-like quantity basis reproduces 17 of 17 with a clean corridor between 8.52 and 10.07 per cent, while window value change misclassifies at least 4 cases under every possible bar, matched value at least 4, the unwalked variant at least 3, chapter-total quantity and mass at least 3 each, exporter-grain quantity at least 2 and matched mass at least 1. The decisive failures sit in cycles where the annex carried nothing, the chapter 12 assessment of 2027Q1 and the chapter 90 assessment of 2027Q2, so the one-entry-per-cycle rule cannot excuse any of them, and exactly one basis survives.

Applied the surviving basis to the open cycle: chapter 22 measures -18.09 per cent, driven by the restructured mid-tier houses withdrawing bulk volume while premium repricing holds the chapter's dollars near flat (window value +1.3 per cent), and 372 exporters ship in both windows so the fall is not entry and exit churn.

Checked chapter 22's own history against the register: its April 2027 assessment measured -6.9 per cent at that window, correctly below the range, and the earlier windows read -0.8 and -1.1, so the movement crossed the bar between April and September and the April no-action row is consistent with designating now.
Recommendation: the annex names chapter 22, and the December-quarter records review is scoped to it.
