steps: Read both despatch feeds and collapsed them to the consignment reference. The Rushden manifest carries 96,303 lines and the Burnley feed 41,561, for 135,403 consignments across the season, because a reprint raises a second line under the same reference.

Removed the consignments in the withdrawal register. Withdrawals run at 3.6 per cent and every one of them is keyed before its collection left the yard, so "withdrawn" and "withdrawn before it was accepted" select the same set.

Set every consignment against the first pull at its own site departing at or after its manifest timestamp, and took the operating day of that pull as its chargeable day. Rushden is collected Monday to Saturday and Burnley Monday to Friday, so a Sunday label at Rushden and a Saturday label at Burnley are both Monday's collection, and on the heavy days both sites work past the last pull.

Validated that construction against the period the carrier has already invoiced: it reproduces all 29 rows of the daily statement for 3 to 22 April exactly, on the count and on the money, ties all 88 driver receipts on their piece counts, and foots to invoice PPN2028041. The label date reproduces none of the 29 rows and is 9.3 per cent light on the statement total.

Checked what the one-cut-per-day model assumes against the agreement, because the yard log's `routed_to` column shows a new destination from 26 April: a late Rushden departure to the carrier's hub on 17 of the window's operating days. Clause 2.3 dedicates hub trunk collections to Consignments on Guaranteed Services, so an N48 or BKY consignment manifested after the last Kettering pull cannot be on the trunk and is accepted the next operating day. The April validation cannot arbitrate this, because no trunk ran before 24 April and the two readings select identical days for every invoiced consignment.

Rebuilt acceptance per service: any pull for N24, PRE and SAT, the next depot pull for N48 and BKY. That moves 5,101 of the window's consignments a day later, off the surcharged Mondays to Wednesdays and Fridays and into the Thursdays and Saturdays that sit under threshold.

Scoped to the uninvoiced part, operating days 24 April to 27 May 2028, 29 at Rushden and 24 at Burnley, and applied clause 5.1 per point per day: the excess over 1,452 at Rushden and 682 at Burnley, priced at the Schedule 3 band for the day of acceptance. Rushden clears its threshold on 18 of 29 operating days and Burnley on 15 of 24. **The surcharge is GBP 16,078.88.**

Built the rest of the carriage on the same set: zones from the matrix issued 6 March 2028, base carriage at Schedule 4 plus GBP 0.88 for each piece beyond the first, fuel at the percentage published at least fourteen days earlier, accrued unrounded and rounded once per collection point, which is the only convention that reproduces invoice PPN2028041's fuel lines to the penny. Base carriage GBP 274,374.37, fuel GBP 32,817.61, total carriage GBP 323,270.86 on 268,833.29 kg.

Ran the clause 6.1 claim off the promised delivery dates the labels carry and the delivery scans, taking the earliest genuine DELIVERED scan per consignment. 4,404 of 46,712 guaranteed consignments missed their promised date and GBP 16,036.57 is claimable.

step_openings: set every consignment against the first
critical_components: Each consignment's chargeable day is constructed, not read: it is the operating day of the first pull the consignment could have left on, built from its manifest timestamp against the yard log, because neither despatch feed records acceptance. The window totals are identical either way (70,380 chargeable consignments), and the daily distribution is completely different.

Which pulls a consignment could have left on depends on its service. Clause 2.3 dedicates the hub trunk running from late April to Guaranteed Services, so on the 17 trunk days a standard consignment's cut is the last depot pull, not the last pull. That moves 5,101 window consignments (7.2 per cent) a day later and is worth GBP 2,907.33 on the surcharge.

The account has two collection points with separate baselines and separate feeds. Burnley is 20,738 of the 70,380 consignments and GBP 6,641.69 of the surcharge, which is 41.3 per cent of it, not the rounding item commercial expected.

Both feeds are at manifest-line grain and the withdrawal register is unmarked in them: the 2,461 reprint lines collapse to their consignment references, and the 4,881 withdrawn consignments (3.6 per cent) carry no charge under clause 4.2, worth GBP 1,986.01 on the surcharge.

The surcharge is a per collection point, per operating day excess over 110 per cent of that point's baseline, priced at the Schedule 3 rate for the day of acceptance, so it is a sum of 29 and 24 separate hinges rather than a rate on a total.
submission.recommendation: We should agree a demand surcharge of **GBP 16,078.88** with Pennine for the uninvoiced part of the 2028 Charging Period, being the operating days from 24 April to 27 May 2028. Rushden carries GBP 9,437.19 of that on 9,296 surcharged consignments and Burnley GBP 6,641.69 on 6,598. steps: Applied the dictionary's minimum-service scope to the panel, keeping enrolment spells that record twelve or more contact hours in total, which lifts the statewide rate from 27.59 to 28.11 per cent in PY2026-27 and from 26.62 to 27.15 in PY2027-28 and leaves the movement at -0.96 percentage points.

Read the contracting records rather than the site master's closing grantee: the agreement history says where and when each instrument applies, the subaward register says who it was executed with, and joining the two shows four Central Ohio sites moving to a new grantee on 1 May 2028, eleven months into the year. Nineteen sites carry a mid-term instrument and only these four change party; the history carries no action or type column, so nothing short of walking each site's chain through the join tells a re-letting from a change of hands.

Rebuilt each participant's enrolment history across sites, which the panel supports because a spell is one continuous run of service at one site and the system issues a new spell on registration at a new site. 1,706 participants leave the four Central Ohio sites over the winter and resume the next month at another operator's Central Ohio site, and clause 4 of the standard terms keeps that service under the subaward of the site they transferred from, so those 5,354 participant-months are Maumee Valley's rather than the receiving operators'. steps: Resolved the retail stack first. The SS27 platform export carries 38,254 live variant rows under 6,200 live listing keys, which is what that file holds and what it says it holds.
Took the parent rows out. A row whose colour is `MULTI` groups a style's colourways and carries no size and no barcode, so it is not a choice: 160 keys.

Took the superseded listing keys out. A relisted garment is issued a new key and the old key stays in the export until the archive sweep, so the live row for a garment is the highest row version for its style and colour: 260 keys. Retail choices live at the extract are 5,780.

Brought in the partner platform, which runs on a separate stack and shares no key with the retail one. Resolved a Collective offer to a choice on the brand's own item code and mapped its free-text colour and size through the crosswalks: 6,470 choices live.

Matched the two stacks on the barcode rather than on the string. Brands send GTIN-13, GTIN-12 with the leading zero dropped and formatted strings with hyphens and spaces, so the digits are the identifier and they pad back to thirteen. That leaves 900 garments carried on both routes, counted once, and 11,350 choices live across both.

Added the listings scheduled to open on or before the season opening date, which the range lock summary puts at Monday 11 January 2027: 1,600 choices. A listing scheduled after that date is certified against the season it opens in, not this one. Choices served at season open are 12,950.

Rebuilt the pattern behind every choice. A style re-coded at a season change is the same pattern as the style it was re-coded from, which the lineage table records, and a Collective listing keeps the brand's own style reference across seasons, so both stacks group back to a pattern and a garment carried on both joins the two through its barcode.

Recovered each pattern's graded scale as the scale whose members are exactly the size labels that pattern has carried, across every colourway and both closed seasons as well as SS27. The scale master resolves each pattern to exactly one scale.
Tested each served choice against its pattern's scale rather than against its own sizes. 3,022 are short, of which 1,331 are missing three or more sizes.
Certified SS27 at 9,928 choices, 73,344 variants behind them.

Two independent live responses filed GBP 130,130 exactly. The v1 post-mortem contributes three results. (1) Composing two governing documents of one instrument is a reading, not a construction: partner agreement 7.4 said a float award IS an award of the Fund and scheme rule 5.2 said the ceiling counts the total awarded, and splitting the fact across two documents bought nothing, because the opponent reads every governing document. A split antidote only works when one half sits somewhere the solver must CONSTRUCT rather than read. (2) A device whose only defence is silence has to be measured against a pack that breaks the silence: task76 v1's ask-layer ceiling was scored at 52.4 assuming the partner-code migration stayed unnamed, and `grants_committee_notes.md` named the renumbering, the float top-ups and the accreditation lapse outright, handing over the B1 device, the decisive rung and rung 2 together. Sweep the social layer against the device ledger before scoring any ceiling. (3) Re-rooting the ASK inside a closed-identity world does not work, and the discriminating test is whether the candidate changes what ONE UNIT of the graded sum is, not which rows enter it or how much each contributes; fifteen candidates were designed and killed on that test, including a ceiling-dial counterfactual measured at 0.8 to 3.3 per cent divergence downward (min is nearly idempotent) and an identical figure upward.

steps: Took the installed base at the extract date and scoped it: 11,447 active units, of which 10,316 sit in a coverage class that carries planned attendance under schedule 1.2.

Dated every unit's next planned visit off the work-order history rather than off the calendar. A unit with a planned maintenance history is due at the applicable interval from its last one; a unit with none is due in the twenty-fourth month after commissioning under schedule 3.1, which takes most of the SY2030 intake out of the window, and SY2030 was the largest intake year the business has had.

Went looking for the interval schedule 2.1 assigns and found no sentence anywhere in the folder that says over what period the duty accumulation is measured. Read the field network's settlement of SY2030 instead: it claims for 2,387 planned work orders in the two districts it works, and the labour band on each claim maps through the rate card to the interval that visit was performed under, so the interval assigned to those units is recoverable.

Ran nine candidate measurement periods forward against the settlement. Measuring across the planned maintenance period, that is between a unit's last two planned visits, reproduces all 2,387 claims exactly. Two further periods are convergent with it by construction and return the same assignments. The remaining six each miss between 13.7 and 23.9 per cent of the claims.

Applied the recovered rule to the whole book, not the settlement's own due rate to it: the two subcontracted districts run at 42.7 per cent of their covered units falling due against 64.3 per cent across the other four, so a rate carried across from the settlement lands at about 2,732 visits. On the recovered rule, 2,620 covered units go onto twenty-four months and are not due again until SY2032, and 7,696 stay on twelve.

Collapsed the 5,877 units falling due inside SY2031 to the delivered grain under schedule 4: **3,642 site visits**, spread 951, 897, 928 and 866 across the four quarters, with Midlands carrying the most at 697 and East of England the fewest at 463.

Not 5,185, which is what those same work orders came to on the site-visit grain the subcontract is actually priced on, and which is 42.4 per cent above the committed figure. And not 4,162, which is what the interval test returns if the duty a unit accumulates is measured from its last service event of any kind rather than across its planned maintenance period.

steps: Read the two facts the Agreement fixes and nothing else: the Wave Minimum for 2029A is 7,677 completed interviews, sample is released in replicates of 500, the authorised release is the smallest whole number of replicates whose forecast completes reach the Minimum, and planning parameters come from the pooled case file of the four most recently closed waves.

Measured eligibility on that pooled file by frame source rather than in aggregate, one rate per frame component over that component's whole pooled record, which is the basis Schedule 3 files and which the Centre may not vary: 0.8680 on MAF, 0.2777 on the address point layer, 0.7546 on the rural route conversions. Applied to the 2029A frame composition this gives 0.6252 eligible per address released, against 0.8516 on the 2028B composition carried forward, so eligibility alone moves the release by a third.

Measured self-response and follow-up conversion by stratum on final dispositions rather than at any wave's published cut. On the matured file 2028B ran a 43.87 per cent response ratio against the 37.27 per cent the methods report publishes, because completed interviews keep arriving through the closeout after the cut.
Applied the 2029A allocation, which moved from near-equal to proportional and puts 20,176 of the 48,500 addresses into Capitol Basin urbanised, the lowest-yielding stratum in the design.

Read the field caseload against the roster. Across the six closed waves the cases ever assigned to follow-up never exceed 11.5 per interviewer-week, and 2026A, 2027A and 2028A reproduce that figure exactly on three different rosters while the other three waves sit below it because their caseloads were smaller than their rosters could take. The 2029A staffing plan of 54 interviewers for eleven weeks therefore takes 6,831 cases.

Solved the release against that ceiling. Below 13,000 addresses every unresolved case is worked and a replicate returns 152.5 completed interviews; above it the worked caseload is fixed and a replicate returns only its 52.3 self-response interviews. The smallest release clearing 7,677 is 97 replicates, 48,500 addresses, landing 7,703.
Recommendation: authorise 48,500 addresses.

steps: Built the enrolment of record at the 1 August 2028 strike date from the spell file: one open spell per student, mapped to the site its school was assigned to on that date. 10,938 students at fourteen approved sites, with the students at the two schools no site covers falling out.

Conformed the two determination sources. The state match is keyed on the state identifier and the household applications on the district identifier, so the match rows resolve through the crosswalk, which carries superseded identifiers as well as active ones. Collapsed the supplemental extract batch against the first on the determination reference.

Applied the Handbook's test: a category on the schedule, in force on the strike date. 3,655 students qualify. Held against the Department's revision notices for the five settled years, this is the same test the notices adjudicate, reason code by reason code.

Read the settled returns as a record of how each site operated. In every site-year the return either served the whole enrolled roster or served at most 0.58 of it, so open operation is an exact signature rather than a judgement. Five sites show open years.

Dated each designation from s.6.4's criterion event rather than from its first open year. The clause designates where the settled referral share of the preceding year reaches 55.0 per cent, and the returns carry those shares: Canfield Park 57.1 in PY2024, Eastgate 58.3 in PY2024, Granger Mill 56.7 in PY2025, Kestrel Ridge 58.2 in PY2027, and nothing else in seventy settled site-years reaches the criterion. Anchoring on first open operation instead fails the clause's own test at two sites: it implies a PY2026 designation for Canfield Park whose reference share settled at 49.2, and a PY2027 designation for Granger Mill whose reference share settled at 52.1. The docket explains the lag both times, the criterion year's revision settled after the following September (Canfield Park's PY2024 on 2024-10-19, Granger Mill's PY2025 on 2025-11-06), so the designation issued after its first term year had opened and that year ran on referral. Ironbridge's run sits on the window edge, s.6.5 dates its designation at or before PY2024, and either way its term ends by PY2027.
Certified each site on the model in force: the whole roster at Granger Mill and Kestrel Ridge, the determination holders everywhere else. 5,195 students.

**The determination test.** 3,655 of those students hold a determination in a category on the Handbook schedule that is in force on the strike date, once the state identifiers are resolved through the crosswalk so a student holding a superseded identifier is counted once, and once the supplemental extract batch is collapsed against the first.

**The designation dating.** A term runs four years from the year of designation, and s.6.4 designates on the criterion event: a settled referral share reaching 55.0 per cent designates the following year. Dated that way, Granger Mill (PY2026 to PY2029) and Kestrel Ridge (PY2028 to PY2031) are in force for PY2029, and Canfield Park (PY2025 to PY2028) and Eastgate (PY2025 to PY2028) have lapsed. Dating terms at the first year open service shows in the returns misdates Canfield Park by a year, because its criterion year settled late and the site worked the first term year on referral.

steps: Read the scheme rules. Rule 3 fixes the measure as filled jobs in the last month of the measurement year less the last month of the base year, taken across all of a firm's PAYE registrations, at the amended schedule where one exists, and it fixes the payee as the firm. Rule 4 fixes the gate: a schedule filed in every month of both years, and net new filled jobs above nil. Rule 5 fixes the two rates and rule 6 the tier in force on the last day of the year.
Built the natural pipeline, one PAYE registration at a time on the schedule as first filed, paying every registration that grew. **NZD 6,153,400.**

Took the amended schedule as the figure for its month. Amendments concentrate in the recent months, so they bear on the closing end harder than the opening end and the figure falls to **NZD 5,014,800.**
Joined the registrations to the register and took each unit's registrations together, so a unit with one site growing and another shrinking is paid on the net. **NZD 4,701,600** across 352 units.

Back-tested that pipeline against the closed pilot, which settled 161 firms and NZD 1,380,000. It reproduces to the dollar. Reading the originals instead misses 46 of the 161 settlements and puts the total 12.7 per cent high; paying registrations without taking them together misses every one of the 161. The pilot pins the measure and it pins the aggregation.

Resolved the unit rule 3 names. A register unit's site set is the set of sites its registrations cover. **203 units closed on a date and 203 units opened the following date filing the identical site set**, one for one, with no unit having a second candidate and no unrelated pair of units anywhere in the register sharing a site set. Those pairs are one firm under rule 3.

Applied rule 4 at the firm. A firm that traded under two numbers filed in every month of both years through one or the other, so it passes the gate; its base is the earlier number's March 2026 and its close the later number's March 2027. **NZD 7,725,800** across 471 firms on 3,169 net new filled jobs.

Cut the committed figure three ways for the committee, each adding back to it: by zone tier per rule 5, by industry division, and by territorial authority through the classification held with the scheme file.

critical_components: A firm's net new filled jobs are its **March 2027 filled jobs less its March 2026 filled jobs**, taken across every PAYE registration it holds, at the **amended** schedule where one was filed.

Rule 3 pays **the firm**. The business register's unit is the registered legal unit, so the two are not the same unit of account, and the unit rule 3 names has to be recovered before rule 4's gate can be applied to it.

**203 firms traded under one registered number at the start of the measurement year and another at the end of it**, filing the identical set of sites under both. Taken as the firm they filed a schedule in every month of both years; taken as two units neither did.
Rule 4's gate therefore admits **119 firms** worth **NZD 3,024,200** that a register-unit reading refuses, and the run reaches 471 firms rather than the 352 a register-unit reading reaches.
submission.recommendation: **The 2027/28 payment run commits NZD 7,725,800, to 471 firms on 3,169 net new filled jobs.** Not NZD 4,701,600, which is what the run comes to when the firm is taken to be a unit on the business register. Not NZD 5,014,800, which is where the figure sits before a firm's PAYE registrations are taken together. Not NZD 6,153,400, which is the natural first pass, one registration at a time on the schedules as first filed.

steps: Built the membership frame from the registry: 24,646 active memberships (17,943 opened in the app, 6,703 created at the June migration), with accounts support closed during the year excluded and their Hazel & Hound history carried by the surviving membership through the link register.

Routed Hazel & Hound accounts to memberships: account links dated on or before December 31 first (the terms fix the run on links as they stood at the close of the year, so the January linking surge stays out), then the provisioned accounts' source references, keeping the account key as a character key because leading zeros are significant.

Conformed the two order systems to one basis: the app stack's JSON orders in dollars with UTC stamps, the Hazel & Hound archive in integer cents with Eastern local stamps, cancelled orders out. The orders frozen in SHIPPED state when the carrier sync ended belong to storefront customers who never joined The Den, so they move the send-off total and no member's year.

Attributed every Hazel & Hound purchase to the member The Den credited it to: the Den ledger posts base points per order to the member's Den number, and joining those postings to the archive on the order reference finds the purchases made at a checkout that never signed in, which sit under customer records outside the link register and the provisioned accounts and would otherwise read as non-member sales. The account routing from step 2 then carries each credited Den number to its membership.

Computed qualifying activity per member: merchandise subtotal of completed 2027 orders plus the credited Hazel & Hound purchases, minus merchandise refunds on returns initiated by January 10 (the Fetchwell returns file, which also holds the late-May storefront orders returned after the switchover, and the storefront returns file, each refund netted against the member whose purchase it reversed). 1,298 members finish at $2,400 or more and 5,048 at $900 to $2,400.

Checked the basis forks the room will bring: the paid read (subtotal less points credits) gives 1,148, the account-only read of the archive gives 1,143, and the ledger reads give 1,448 and 1,590, each for a reason named in block 4.
Split the 1,298 by box build from the pet profile of record: 749 dog, 353 cat, 196 other, every Top Dog member resolving to exactly one primary species.

Filled the closing block from the same conformed layers: the Hazel & Hound send-off figures netted of every return of those sales, and the winback list off the ledger of record under the export manifest's batch rules, both stated in block 5.

steps: Built January and May on the KPI sheet's basis: invoiced prospecting spend (Anvil's 9 to 10 May delivery credit and Prism's rebate netted, Corridor's 12% fee included, re-engagement out), network impressions and clicks with Corridor taken from its invoiced delivery lines, Tessellate installs counted once per device and install time, trials and first-ever payments from the store with the pre-cutover archive and the 14-day refund window applied, everything on Denver days and credited through the install of record. January $222,400.62 over 1,726 new payers is $128.85; May $342,870.59 over 2,030 is $168.90.

Walked the change one factor at a time in the KPI sheet's order: cost per thousand impressions +$24.16, impressions per click -$0.36, clicks per install +$0.47, installs per trial +$6.32, trials per new payer +$9.47. The price of impressions is most of the rise.
Tested the loudest dated change: Anvil iOS prospecting cost per thousand rose 9.8% across 6 March, but campaigns that never switched rose 4.0% over the same fortnight, leaving 5.6% for value bidding.

Grouped every prospecting campaign by network, platform, age band and the set of metros on its geo list: 49 sets hold two or three live campaigns at the extract, the second and third launched from October with fresh creative and ramped by routine budget raises. They carried 17.1% of Anvil and Prism prospecting spend in January and 62.0% in May.

Priced a live copy from the change log: seven 2027 pauses whose budget moved at the same timestamp to a campaign with identical targeting. The survivor's cost per thousand fell to 78.0% of its previous level each time, 1.2814 on average over 14-day windows, with click-through unmoved; three pauses whose budget moved to a different age band in the same metros, and nine large budget raises on campaigns without a copy, moved nothing.

Checked the other readings against the same data: same-metro campaigns without a copy priced 7.3% higher in May than January, copied ones 29.8%; Spring 28 click-through decays on Winter 28's curve; 4.2 trials converted at 31.1% against 33.5% on older versions during the rollout.
Applied the change to May: removing the premium on the contested impressions with spend held puts May at $149.77 per new payer, $150 to the nearest ten dollars.
Recommendation: merge the copied campaigns on 1 July, 50 pauses and 49 budget changes, longest-running campaign kept in every set.

submission.domain_tag: Product Analytics, acquisition & growth (bounty-paid acquisition partners; partner and affiliate channels, marketing attribution).
submission.objective_tag: Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics (separating a real event from an artifact).
steps: Took the rule from the Partner Programme Quality Policy. Section 2 defines a member's pay dates as the dates their employer pays them, and payroll activation counts payroll that lands by the second of those dates a deposit instruction given on the opening day could reach. The October review assesses the May and June 2026 cohorts (the two latest months ninety days past their last day at the 2 October extract), a partner breaches in a month below 0.85 of the programme's payroll activation, placement needs a breach in both months with at least 150 members after exclusions, and the lowest pooled ratio breaks a tie.

Recovered provider lead times from the switch events, reading each submission's day as the date written in its timestamp and counting business days from the next business day when that day is a weekend or holiday, as the data dictionary does: Halden HCM 10 business days, Cascade Paysuite 5, the rest 1 to 3, each an exact threshold (no confirmed switch ever reaches a pay date closer than its provider's lead).

Put every member on their own pay group by matching the confirmed effective pay date to the employer's calendars: 106 of Harborline's 427 review-cohort openers are off their employer's primary group, 102 of them on a monthly management group, and 433 of ShiftBridge's 951 on a weekly hourly group.

Took each linked member's hire date from the employment records and each pay date's pay period from the calendars, and counted as the member's pay dates only those whose period ends on or after the hire date, because the data dictionary says a pay date pays the employees who worked in that period: 270 of ShiftBridge's review-cohort openers were hired after they opened, 245 of them onto the weekly hourly groups. Start dates fall on the first day of a pay period, so counting periods the member worked in and periods wholly after the hire gives the same dates.

Found each member's first qualifying payroll that landed (one employer's credits combined per day, at least $200, returned credits out and a duplicate delivery counted once, as section 2 sets out) and the second of the member's pay dates that a deposit instruction given on the opening day could have reached: a pay date the provider's lead or more business days after the opening day. Applied to each member's own confirmed switch, that clock puts all 156,351 on exactly their confirmed effective pay dates.

Excluded the 731 Pocketfare openers, and 232 across the other partners, who opened in Nevada between 4 May and 28 June while switching was paused, then scored every partner: no assessed partner is under the floor in both months, ShiftBridge comes nearest at 61.4 and 60.4 per cent against the programme's 64.7 and 66.0, and Fieldhand is not assessed. The counts behind those four figures are 294 of 479 and 267 of 442 for ShiftBridge, against 2643 of 4083 and 2655 of 4025 across all partner-attributed openers, every cohort after the Nevada exclusion.

Back-tested the measure on the review register: it reproduces all 109 filed dispositions across the eight closed reviews. Counting every scheduled pay date of the group, which is the same clock without the hire dates, gets six of the eight reviews wrong (9 rows): it places Moneyline Podcast in 2024-Q4 instead of CareRoster, RideNest in 2025-Q1 instead of Brightcredit and Civic Ledger in 2025-Q3 instead of RideNest, and places CareRoster in 2025-Q4, Campus Ledger in 2026-Q1 and Fieldhand in 2026-Q2, three reviews that placed nobody. Counting pay dates on or after the hire date gets four wrong (5 rows). The 14, 30, 45 and 60 day windows misclassify 9, 9, 8 and 5 rows, and the first or third pay date 7 and 2.

Worked the margin on the nearest partner: ShiftBridge would have to lose 34 payroll-activated May openers and 22 June ones, the programme's counts falling with them, for each month to fall below the floor. Losing 34 takes May to 260 of 479 against the programme's 2609 of 4083, the first loss that puts the month under 0.85, and losing 22 takes June to 245 of 442 against 2633 of 4025.

Worked the bounty side under the agreement (qualifying payroll effective within 60 days of opening, the tier set by the month's clause 3.1 funded accounts, first membership per person, no fraud-review closure inside 60 days, no partner on probation for a May or June cohort) against the latest accepted statement for each partner and month: the statements of record sit $18,045 above what May and June openers earned.
Recommendation: place no partner on probation for November through January.

steps: Built the senior population from the enrolment spans rather than the student record: a 2027-28 senior is a student whose eleventh-grade enrolment was still open at the pull, reported at the school that enrols them, which is operations note 1.3. That is 761 students.

Computed each one's shortfall against Board Policy 218 area by area, counting a repeated course once (s.2.1) and subtracting what the senior timetable itself carries (operations note 2.2): 286 seniors are short in at least one area, and 251 of them owe at most one credit in every area they are short in, which is what a section delivering one credit per student per year (note 1.2) can clear.
Read the 2027-28 sections off the recovery schedule: 36 year-term sections, six per school, the places each carries, and the period each meets in. The funded year has no summer section.

Ran the walk the operations note files with every section's places unlimited, one place per area per year and one place per period: **221** of the 286 could be brought to a diploma by the schedule as it stands, and 65 could not, 35 because they owe more than one credit in an area and 30 because the two areas they owe both meet in period 3.

Ran the same walk with the funded places, over all 286 short seniors, most credits outstanding first then student number, offering each student one place in each area they are short in, the area they owe most in first and level areas in Policy 218's order, only where the section still had a place open, and letting a student hold one place per period, so the second of two period 3 offers is not taken and goes on down the order. Counted the students holding every credit they owed at the end of it: **102**. 29 offers were declined because the student already held a place meeting in that period, 124 offers were refused because the section was full, and 12 of the 36 sections turned at least one student away.
Took the difference school by school: the funded places ran out for 119 of the 221, 42 of them at Raystown.

Ran the funded walk three more ways to place the rivals: every offered place taken, 121; the seniors a place cannot bring to the schedule left out of the walk, 143; both, 166. A free allocation ignoring the filed order reaches 192 without the periods and 186 with them.

submission.domain_tag: Economics, public finance (tax statistics, a city's transient guest tax revenue estimate).
submission.objective_tag: Forecasting & Predictive Modeling (a predicted value for a fiscal year that has not opened, pinned by the supplied history).
steps: Read what the line is and how the base is built. The estimating notes define the line as the tax the tournaments add to the year's receipts, and set the base as the latest twelve months of total receipts carried month for month, with the prior year's tournament tax taken out of the month it arrived in and nothing added for growth in rooms or rates.

Placed the window. Returns fall due by the 20th of the month after the stay (610.330) and the receipts report books cash in the month received, so FY2027 receipts are the tax on stays from September 2026 to August 2027, which covers 1,062 block nights across 39 tournaments in the Bureau's pace and 26,441 contracted rooms.

Priced pickup with the Bureau's filed method, rooms picked up over rooms contracted across the FY2024 and FY2025 close-outs, which is 0.9031 for REQUIRED tournaments and 0.5792 for RECOMMENDED ones. Priced at the group rate and taxed at 7 percent, every block in the window comes to $184,104, which is the careful stopping point.

Stood every block night on the same weekday a year earlier in the district's nightly census, and took the hotel's regular rooms that night (rooms sold less the close-out pickup) against its rooms available. Of the 1,062 block nights, 144 (7,513 contracted rooms, 6,784.6 expected to be picked up) fall on nights the hotel sold every room on regular business, and they are exactly the championship series' Friday and Saturday nights and the Lake Showdown's weekend, while every other block night leaves its hotel at or under 92 percent. Standing the nights on the same date instead (365 days back) gives the identical result, because every City property sells out every summer Thursday, Friday and Saturday at one flat rate.

Valued each night. A night with rooms to spare adds the pickup times the group rate times 7 percent, and a sold-out night adds the pickup times the group rate less that hotel's regular rate that night, times 7 percent, which is negative. The invitationals add $125,371, the championship series takes $67,916 (all of it in July 2027 receipts) and the Lake Showdown takes $6,535 (June 2027 receipts), so the line is $50,919.63, carried to the nearest hundred as $50,900.

Built the full year. steps: Read the programme guidelines. Section 4 places the award with the applicant whose unrestricted net assets fall to nil or below earliest inside the award term, counting the payments its other funders have contracted to make in that term, and section 5 sets the award at the deepest that applicant's balance is carried below nil at any month end of the term, capped at what the Trustees voted. Section 3 fixes the term at twelve months from 1 July 2026 and carries the close the cycle's watch list is published for into the start of it, so the roll opens on the May 2026 balance at the first term month end and there is no month in between to account for.

Took the twelve applicants from the 2026 application file and confirmed every one appears on the monitor's May watch list, which section 2 requires before an organisation can be considered. All twelve qualify and none of the three prior stabilisation awards went to any of them, so the four-cycle rule in section 1 excludes nobody.
Pulled the unrestricted balance series out of the monthly returns and the signed payment schedules out of the commitment register, and put them on the same monthly grid.

Recovered what each organisation's own operations consume. The returns record expense and never record income, so the change in the balance is a net figure with the funders' money already in it, and the operating gap is that month's scheduled support less that month's movement. It comes to the same figure in every month of the series, so nothing turns on how far back the window is taken: three months, twelve, or the whole fifty-nine return the same gap for every applicant.

Rolled each balance forward across the twelve months of the term, adding what the schedules pay in that month and taking out the gap, and read off the first month end at or below nil. Peacham crosses in September 2026, Craftsbury in November 2026, Chelsea in February 2027, and the other nine come through the term.

Checked the ordering is not an artifact of the roll. The nine that come through end the term at nine different balances, from 24,000 up to 219,000 US dollars, so the field is strictly ordered with no tie to break, and reading section 4's "nil or below" strictly instead returns the same placement and the same sum.

Took the minimum of Peacham's twelve projected month-end balances. It is 330,000 US dollars below nil at the February 2027 month end, five months after the crossing and one month before the first of its two 2027 instruments pays.
Recommendation: the award is written for 330,000 US dollars, against the 750,000 the Trustees voted to the Fund.

steps: Read the programme document and the denomination reference to fix the schedule: three waves, the third covering the 500 and the 1000 with the window running the whole of 2027, an order committed once for the production year, and a closing reserve of two months of that year's issuance.

Built the print-run ledger from the two registers, outstanding by run as first issues less notes destroyed, which the dictionary licenses by defining a destruction as happening once. Outstanding S04 at the 2026 position date is 41,800,000 of the 500 and 12,400,500 of the 1000.

Took the pooled realised return of the four settled conversions, 93.38 per cent, and checked it against the twin pair before using it. The 50 and the 100 converted in the same wave, on the same window and the same announcement lead, and their whole outstanding stock was handled 2.981 and 2.992 times in the year before the window, within 0.4 per cent of each other. They returned 84.0 and 97.1 per cent. One pooled share cannot be right for both, so the pooled transfer is dead.

Tested the obvious replacement, each denomination's own return rate over a one-year window as `1 - exp(-turnover)`. It fails on the 200, handled 0.869 times in the year before its window, so the model allows 58.1 per cent at most and 93.0 per cent actually came in. Changeover presentation is not the ordinary return process.

Split the stock by print run instead, and tested the two obvious ways of drawing the line against the settled conversions. Taking the residue to be the 2004 to 2007 build-up and nothing else does not fit: it implies a dormant presentation rate of 0.0108 and still misses a settled conversion by 1.93 points of stock, because the 50 and the 200 each have a later run that stopped being destroyed years ago.

Took the residue to be every run with no destruction recorded in the last three years. That fits all four settled conversions exactly, at 0.1784, and it is wrong on this wave, because the settled denominations stopped printing years before their windows while the S04 500 and 1000 were kept in print to 2026 while the wave was held. Five runs of each therefore carry no destructions at all.

Separated the two cases on the register's own evidence. Every run of every denomination in the pack begins its destruction stream at the same age for that denomination, five years for the 500 and the 1000, and the 500's 2021 run began its stream in 2026 exactly on that schedule. A run printed in 2023 with nothing destroyed is inside that lag. A dormant run is one that ran and stopped, and both wave denominations have one in the middle of the live block, the 500 in 2015 and the 1000 in 2013 and 2015, with live runs on both sides of it, so no cut on age separates the two pools.

Solved the four settled conversions for the presentation law on that split. Added the reserve, took off the issuable holding, and rounded to the thousand as the prompt requires: 27,747 thousand of the 500, 5,459 thousand of the 1000, 33,206 thousand in total, 3,194 thousand inside the contracted annual capacity.

Rebuilt the settled wave from the lodgement ledger, which needed two things before any cell could be added up. The extract holds every copy of every row that was ever transmitted, up to four copies of one centre month, and validation runs a reporting month at a time, so the copy of record is the one from the last transmission whose month was taken rather than the newest copy on the row. Then each centre's month is counted against the depot that held it in that month rather than the depot the extract carries, which is the assignment as it stands at the pull. Both readings are needed: the accepted copy attributed to the extract's depot column rebuilds nothing, and the newest copy attributed to the depot of the month rebuilds nothing either.

steps: Took the discharge lifts out of the 89,191 row terminal move log and kept the 3,521 containers landed between 1 January and 31 March 2028, of which 2,717 belong to the sixteen major accounts.

Built completion of discharge per call as the latest discharge lift on that call, then priced both clocks off the tariff: demurrage from the day after completion to the gate, detention from the day after the gate to the empty return, each on its own banded scale. Tariff 4.1 counts the bands from the first chargeable day of the charge concerned, so a clock the place shortens is priced again from its own day one rather than having the saved days struck off the top band. Ranking the sixteen on what they cost gives GBP 1,455,794 and names M02, M01, M06 and M03.

Checked the arithmetic against the two settled years: the 28,400 invoice rows reproduce to GBP 24,931,505 on the same tariff, and the corpus's own heaviest four accounts are the same M02, M01, M06 and M03, so the settled record certifies the desk's ranking exactly.

Modelled a place as collecting every container on the day its free time expires, which removes GBP 824,746 and names M02, M06, M03 and M08. Applied the schedule's three collections a day, which cuts that to GBP 579,764 and names M06, M05, M03 and M12, because a call's containers share one free time start and a block of them cannot clear in a day.

Netted the transfer between the clocks. An earlier gate out does not move the empty return: the return sits 1.77 days wide about the call's completion against 2.60 days about the collection, measured within each account, and a pass-through of +0.0128 over 2,714 containers, grouped by call and account, against 1.0000 for a fixed turnaround. So every day off the demurrage clock is a day on the detention clock, and the figure falls to GBP 307,028 on M05, M08, M12 and M14.

Recovered each account's delivery days from the record, because schedule 1.2 makes a collection a delivery to the premises on the day it is taken and names no days. Across the whole move log the sixteen accounts gate out on between three and seven weekdays each and never once on any other, and the job log gives the identical seven day pattern for all sixteen. Reworked the queue on each account's own days, which carries a container past a day the place does not have rather than collecting on it, and the figure falls to GBP 255,732 on M08, M12, M14 and M10.
Recommendation: fill the four places with M08, M12, M14 and M10, worth GBP 255,732 over the quarter.

The place's collection date is a construction, not a lookup: 3 collections a day worked in order of the day free time expires, against the containers that would otherwise stand past their last free day, with the containers a full day cannot take carried to the following days in the same order, and the whole queue stopping at the quarter end.

The empty return does not move when the collection moves, so the days taken off the demurrage clock are added to the detention clock: GBP 379,802 comes off demurrage and GBP 124,070 goes on to detention.

A collection under a place is a delivery to the account's premises the same day, so the days a place has are the days that account takes delivery, and no file says which those are. The record does: over the whole move log an account's containers are never gated out on a day it does not receive, and the sixteen accounts run from three days a week to seven. Working the queue on each account's own days rather than on all seven moves 13 of the 16 account figures and takes the committed total from GBP 307,028 to GBP 255,732.

steps: Scoped to work the Agreement covers (clauses 3.1, 3.2 and 14.3): the 78 sites on the Agreement in the site register, in the year measured, 29 June 2026 to 27 June 2027.

Priced all 273,281 roster shifts. Schedule B lists its multipliers by day and time and says nothing about a shift that runs past midnight; Ardenvale's sample reproduces 364 of 364 fortnights when a shift takes the band it starts in for all of its hours, and each of seven readings that splits a shift at midnight misses 97 to 333 of them. Covered work in the year measured is 841,516 penalty-weighted hours, and the rate base is $29.42 an ordinary hour.

Read each member's pay off the returns, using ordinary and penalty wages only (the laundry allowance is paid on top under clause 23.1 and the five one-off payments sit outside the rate under clause 24.1). For most members, wages over penalty-weighted hours is one figure in every return row: a rate, with the Schedule B multipliers on it. For 41 member and classification cells in the security stream, at nine members, it is not, and wages over flat units (ordinary hours once, overtime at its multiplier) is: one rate for every hour, whatever the day. That pay is lawful only because clause 20.4 lets pay above what the Agreement requires count towards what it requires in the same pay period, so for those crews the test is each employee's fortnight.

Checked the method against the Secretariat's own costing of the July 2026 adjustment (Costing note 2026/4): run on the 2025-26 year it reproduces all fourteen classifications and the 24.57 cent total to the cent. It would have done so whether or not the one-rate crews were found, because in 2025-26 every one of their rates sat at least 3.6 per cent clear of what its worst fortnight needed, so the 3.5 per cent adjustment left no fortnight short.

Costed every tenth from nothing to 6.0 per cent, each Schedule A rate raised and rounded under clause 20.6: own-rate members owe the raised rate less their own where it falls below, on penalty-weighted hours; the one-rate crews owe, in each pay period, whatever their pay falls short of the raised rates' entitlement for that period's shifts (clause 20.5 puts a shift in the period it starts).

The curve crosses 40 cents between 4.7 per cent (39.4) and 4.8 (40.6). The offer is 4.7 per cent, 33.77 cents of it on own-rate members and 5.59 on the one-rate crews. The union's 6.0 per cent would add 55.7 cents.

Counted the people behind it. Every shift went to the register row whose dates hold it; shifts under a payroll number from before its current holder was engaged belong to an earlier holder, who is someone else because a member gives anyone it re-engages a new number. Rows are one person where a register links them or the name and date of birth match. That gives 720 people across the region in the comparison year, 724 in the year measured and 634 in both, and the district counts in section 5.

steps: Recovered the age at first thinning for all 10,563 stands by joining the stand register's planting year to the earliest thinning licence each stand holds in the felling licence register. Measured sawlog yield by class over the four settled years of delivery records: 0.7695 for the on-time class, 0.2894 for the late class. Blended over those same four years the two come to 0.6994, which is what the Board's own conversion carries.

Built the 2027 harvest base at 3,184,926 cubic metres, 2,377,913 from the public felling programme and 807,013 from private clearfell licences, each licence falling to the year it commences under Article 5.3 of the Levy Order.

In the 2027 base they are 62.92 per cent, so the blend may not be carried and the determination is made class by class.

Carried the two physical conversions off the four settled years taken together, as Article 5.2 requires: delivered volume ran at 1.1152 times the volume programmed and licensed for those years, and the mills sawed 0.4961 cubic metres for every cubic metre of sawlog they took in.

Added the 228,400 cubic metres of sawlog contracted for 2027 delivery from outside the programme, which converts at mill recovery only because it arrives already as sawlog, and which the levy reaches under Article 3.1 whatever the roundwood's origin.
Result: 936,991 cubic metres, 937,000 to the nearest thousand, against 1,053,804 sawn in 2025.
Put the quarterly path together from each unit's own timing: the programme quarter for a programmed stand, the commencement quarter for a licensed one, the delivery window for a contract.

That mill is identified rather than assumed: carrying its declaration to green is what closes the 15,679 cubic metre gap between the returns of record and the published registered total, and it closes it for exactly one mill on the register, the runner-up missing by 3,157 cubic metres. critical_components: The 2027 harvest base is **3,184,926 cubic metres**: 2,377,913 of public felling programme and 807,013 of private-estate clearfell licences commencing in the year.

Sawlog yield splits by the age a stand was first thinned. Stands first thinned at 17 to 22 years yield **0.7695** of delivered volume as sawlog; stands first thinned at 29 years or later, or never thinned, yield **0.2894**. No stand on the register was first thinned between 23 and 28 years.

submission.recommendation: The Board should determine the 2027 levy base at **937,000 cubic metres of sawn timber**. The nearest defensible rival is 828,000 cubic metres, 11.7 per cent away. Not 1,075,000, which is what the Board's pre-amendment practice gives, its sector conversion applied to the 2027 felling programme. Not 1,232,000, which is that conversion once the private clearfell licences are counted at their real 2027 level. Not 1,346,000, which is that figure with the contracted sawlog added. Not 828,000, which is the corrected conversion applied to a base that still carries private volume at its historical proportion.

steps: Read the legacy billing archive (225,766 fund credits, 2000-01 to 2024-25) to customers and service addresses through the account conversion (141,606 legacy accounts), and appended the platform's 25,279 grants for 2025-26 and 2026-27. One grant per customer per season holds throughout, and every published season's customers and renewals tie to the close-out.
Counted, for every grant, how many grants its service address had carried in its life, every tenant, this one included.

Fixed what the planning rates are against last year's schedule, because the method note says rates are struck statewide on the five most recent settled seasons but not which rates. On base seasons 2020-21 to 2024-25 I struck one rate for addresses below three lifetime grants (19.9 per cent, 6,751 of 33,969) and one at three or more (75.0 per cent, 14,365 of 19,142). Applied to each 2025-26 customer and rounded up to the whole renewal, they give back every figure sent on 21 October 2026, at exact or three-decimal rates: Alma 420, Big Rapids 382, Cadillac 434, Coldwater 411, Hastings 482, Ionia 539, Mount Pleasant 595, Owosso 661, St. Johns 502, Three Rivers 485, which is 4,911 renewals and 49 caseworkers. One statewide rate misses all ten, by 2 to 14 renewals at the exact 39.76 per cent (4,952 renewals and 50 caseworkers). Of 17 rival readings, none gives back more than one district: one rate on the five settled seasons, the latest one or every one, district rates, the five customer-history classes, the customer's own grants at the address, and the address count with the customer's own grants left out, on trailing windows, at thresholds two and four, or read as of the roster season.

Tested what brings a customer back. In every base season from 2011-12 to 2025-26 the renewal rate splits on the address count: 19.1 to 21.0 per cent below three grants at the address and 73.8 to 76.4 at three or more, with nothing in between (19.8 and 20.0 at one and two grants, 74.9 at three, 75.3 at four, 75.8 at five, 74.6 at six or more). Inside either class the household's own grant count moves the rate by at most 1.05 points, and 7,196 customers with three or more grants of their own who lived at a short-history address renewed at 19.3 per cent.

Struck the PY2028 planning rates on the five most recent settled seasons together, as the method note requires (base seasons 2021-22 to 2025-26): 19.9 per cent (7,120 of 35,843) and 74.8 per cent (15,040 of 20,099).

steps: Took the extract's 43,975 grant rows, kept positive amounts in pounds, and counted each grant once under the method note's rule (a row repeating the identifier, recipient and amount of one already counted is the same grant published again), which drops William Grant Foundation grants that appear in two of its half-year files and keeps the Historic Environment Scotland and National Churches Trust rows that reuse an identifier for a different amount.

Reproduced rounds one and two from the extract: with population shares for the Scotland-wide money and the release current when each line was set (mid-2023, mid-2024), all eight top-ups on the partners' statements come out to the pound, round one's line at £9.60 and round two's at £11.10. Of 432 variants of time rule, place order, sharing key, duplicate rule and release, only this set reproduces all eight (with either reading of the duplicate rule), six reproduce four and the other 424 reproduce none.

steps: From `office_actions_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` took each docket's decision notice (its one NOA, REF or ABN action; GRT follows an allowance and decides nothing) and its first action on the merits (earliest EXR by `served_on`, then `action_id`), whose `credit_class` (1N or 1R) comes from `examiner_production_ledger_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` on `action_id`.

Read each CX edge in `docket_links.csv` by its successor's class: 1R is the same application re-examined after its refusal was set aside, and 1N is a continuing application filed on the successor's `docketed_on`, because the production standard credits 1N once per application, so a second 1N inside one CX chain would be a second application and the parent's refusal was never set aside (chaining every CX edge reads these successors as re-examinations); a benefit claim does not move the filing date (charter), and CN and DV children are applications of their own.

FY2022 applications are the dockets in `examination_dockets_FY2016_FY2026.parquet` with `docketed_on` from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022 that are not CX children, plus the CX children there whose first action on the merits is credited 1N: 66,186.

Final decision: from the application's docket follow each CX edge unless the successor's first action on the merits is credited 1N, and take the decision notice of the docket reached; where the next successor is credited 1N the decision is the refusal on the docket it leaves, a successor with no first action at the extract leaves the application waiting, and no notice by 30 September 2026 is still waiting at the extract (charter), so a docket's own notice or a transfer is never the end of a re-examined application: 10.6% undecided, none under 1,461 days.

Days from `docketed_on` to the final decision, Kaplan-Meier with the undecided censored at the extract, months as days over 30.4375 (charter), timing applications rather than the dockets Table P1 times: median 880 days, 28.9 months.

Recommendation: the headline prints 28.9 months.

steps: Conformed each holder's latest return for a quarter up to 2026T2 in `declaracions_grans_tenidors_2024T3_2026T2.csv` per `guia_presentacio_declaracio_trimestral_2024-01.pdf` (an S return replaces the return it refers to, a C return adds its lines, a holder with no 2026T2 return stands on its latest earlier quarter), kept PD lines only, expanded parcel lines (the pre-April 2026 format, `avis_portal_canvi_format_2026-03.eml`) to one dwelling per `unitats` charge in `cadastre_habitatges_extracte_20260928.csv`, and resolved each unmatched reference, separators removed and upper-cased, to the one cadastre reference with the same first 18 characters: the 30 June counts tie to `butlleti_parc_residencial_2026T2.pdf` in all 14 sections.

Rolled every dwelling to 1 January 2027 per Article 2.4 of `ordre_designacio_seccions_grans_tenidors.pdf`: deeds in `escriptures_inscrites_2024-07_2026-09.csv` executed after 30 June and registered by 30 September applied in execution order, then notified sales not yet executed passed on `data_transmissio_prevista` if on or before 1 January 2027; a buyer listed in the register's Titulars sheet without `data_baixa` becomes the holder, any other buyer takes the dwelling out of the count.

Read the agency's commitments from `EPPR_execucio_pressupost_2026_gen-set.csv` (programme PPO, phase D, concept naming a tempteig, reference after "RC"), whose 27 purchases already in the deed extract were each executed 120 days after the D line and none on the notified date, and moved each committed sale to the agency 120 days after commitment instead of to its agreed buyer and date (the agency is not a large holder, Article 2.1), stopping the same roll at each month end for the bridges: 4625001012 falls to 183 and 0301402014 keeps the December sales completing 13 to 22 January, at 155.

Added the holders on the `Titulars` sheet of `registre_grans_tenidors_20261001.xlsx` with no return in the returns file (four, inscribed July to September 2026), each holding the dwellings whose latest deed in the extract names it as buyer (Articles 2.1 and 2.4): Habitatges Cornisa SL holds 18 in 4625011016, which reaches 168, and Pòrtic Residencial SL holds 5 in 4625001005 and 6 in 4625013021.

Divided each section's count by its `Residencial` units in the cadastre extract and applied Article 4's 25 per cent: seven sections designated; the distance to the line is taken from the unrounded share.

Largest group: each holder mapped to the group code of its `Vinculacions` link in `registre_grans_tenidors_20261001.xlsx` in force on 1 January 2027 (start on or before, end blank or on or after), named through `codis_grup.csv`, a holder in no group counted alone.

Dwellings with nobody registered: the latest delivery per district in `padro_lliurament_2026-09.csv`, else `padro_lliurament_2026-06.csv` (València districts 11 and 12, Alacant district 2), occupied when a per-dwelling row has `persones` above 0 or a per-person row is live, a TIE-T or PAS registration lapsing two years after the later of `data_alta` and `data_ultima_renovacio` against the delivery's reference day, the 1st of its month (`nota_intercanvi_padro_rev2.txt`).
